1	# Clean-Room Reverse-Engineering Notes: Three NOSIBLE Blog Posts
2	
3	Educational replica notes for a cybernaut_mini-style project. Sources are the three archived posts under `/Users/neelanpather/dev/cybernaut_mini/docs/blog-archive/`.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Post 1: Point-in-Time Knowledge Graphs over Named Entities with NOSIBLE World
8	
9	**Source:** `point-in-time-knowledge-graphs-over-named-entities.md` (published 2026-07-16, "NOSIBLE Research", 8 min read)
10	
11	### 1. WHAT IT IS
12	
13	A pipeline that builds **point-in-time knowledge graphs** over named entities extracted from a de-duplicated global news-event database (NOSIBLE World). Nodes are NER entities (companies, people, products, places); edges are inferred from statistical co-mention **lift** within a single year's news; every edge is date-bucketed so a graph "as of 2018" contains only information knowable in 2018. The problem it solves is **lookahead bias** in backtesting: conventional knowledge graphs accumulate future facts into past views (e.g., a 2007 model "knowing" the iPhone will succeed), which invalidates historical evaluation. The point-in-time construction makes the graph safe to backtest by construction.
14	
15	### 2. ARCHITECTURE
16	
17	Ordered data flow as disclosed:
18	
19	1. **Event database (NOSIBLE World)** — the article stream is collapsed into *one record per real event* (regardless of how many outlets covered it). Each record carries: date, NER entities (with per-name mention counts, grouped by type), resolved company tickers (EODHD format, plus ISIN/LEI/FIGI), coverage counts (total_coverage, total_netlocs = distinct publishers), sentiment + materiality signals, a semantic embedding of the event's meaning, a 20-facet ontology (GICS, IPTC, NOSIBLE event types among them), and per-publisher provenance.
20	2. **NER layer** — NER runs over every event; many entity types recorded; the post uses five: `ORG`, `PERSON`, `GPE`, `LOC` (places), `PRODUCT`.
21	3. **Event selection** — scan every daily slice for the study window (2015 → mid-2026), pull events whose resolved tickers include the target company.
22	4. **Entity canonicalization** — surface forms collapsed ("Apple", "Apple Inc.", "apple" → one node); a lone surname folds into the fuller name kept that year.
23	5. **Yearly co-mention counting** — bucket every event by its document date's year; per (company, year, entity) count events co-mentioning both. No cumulative or forward-looking state — point-in-time by construction.
24	6. **Edge scoring by lift** — compare the co-mention rate against the entity's background rate in the same year's whole corpus. A normalized version of lift is used for ranking so a strong link on a rare product ranks alongside one on a common name.
25	7. **Edge filtering** — ubiquitous entities (e.g., "United States") get lift ≈ 1.0 and fall away; high-lift edges kept.
26	8. **Validation** — sample edges at random, pull the underlying source documents, verify all fall inside the edge's year.
27	9. **Visualization** — (a) per-year force-directed network: nodes = entities co-mentioned with the target; edges join entities that also co-occur *with each other* so related nodes cluster; node color = category, node size = association strength. (b) Evolution matrix (entity × year): dot size = that year's association strength; dot color = year-over-year change in the entity's share of the company's coverage (green grew / white flat / red shrank).
28	
29	### 3. CONCRETE TECHNICAL FACTS
30	
31	- Coverage of NOSIBLE World: **38 thousand tickers, 3.2 million organizations, 6.4 million people**.
32	- Entity types used: **ORG, PERSON, GPE, LOC, PRODUCT** (of "many" recorded types).
33	- Core formula (exact): `lift = (co / target_events) / (entity_events / total_events)`; lift 1.0 = chance; higher = stronger-than-chance association.
34	- Worked lift example (exact numbers): NVIDIA–Blackwell 2024: `co=69`, `target_events=2651` (NVIDIA's 2024 events), `entity_events=75` (Blackwell events in whole corpus that year), `total_events=2249039` → lift ≈ **780** ("roughly 780 times chance").
35	- A **normalized lift** is used before ranking (formula not given).
36	- Canonicalization rules disclosed: case/suffix collapsing ("Apple, Apple Inc. and apple collapse to one node"); "a lone surname folds into the fuller name kept that year" (year-scoped alias resolution).
37	- Point-in-time enforcement: edges bucketed on **document date**, scored against **same-year background**, "no cumulative or forward-looking state".
38	- Validation numbers: **24 of 24** randomly sampled edges verified in-year, "across 955 real documents".
39	- Study corpus: every daily slice **2015 to mid-2026**; events mentioning NVIDIA, Apple, or Coca-Cola: **88,359 total**; **332 distinct products** for NVIDIA, **274** for Apple; "hundreds" of people/orgs/places each.
40	- Sample event record (Microsoft/Activision, 2022-01-18): fields `event.date`, `event.title`, `event.country`; `signals.sentiment="positive"`, `signals.materiality_score=0.83`; `coverage.total_coverage=2740`, `coverage.total_netlocs=2392`; `entities` = per-type dict of name→mention count (e.g., `"Microsoft": 202`, `"Bobby Kotick": 22`, `"Call of Duty": 20`); `tickers` = list of `{name, ticker_eodhd}` (e.g., `MSFT.US`, `ATVI.US`, `6758.TSE`).
41	- Full records additionally carry: event embedding, twenty-facet ontology (GICS, IPTC, NOSIBLE event types), per-publisher provenance, ticker identifiers ISIN/LEI/FIGI.
42	- Reference Python (given in full in the post's appendix):
43	  - `co_mentions_by_year(events, target_ticker, entity_type)` → `defaultdict(Counter)` keyed by `event["date"][:4]`, counting each entity name once per event (presence, not mention count).
44	  - `lift(co, target_events, entity_events, total_events)` → the formula above.
45	- Qualitative results disclosed: NVIDIA 2024 network clusters = memory/foundry supply chain, accelerator platform (GeForce/GPU/Blackwell), AI cloud (Microsoft/Google/OpenAI), peers (AMD/Intel). Product timeline: RTX 2018, DLSS 2019, A100 2020, Blackwell/HBM/H200 2024. Apple: Watch/AirPods mid-2010s, iPhone X 2018, AirPods Pro/Pro Max from 2019, AirTag/Dynamic Island later, Vision Pro 2025. Coca-Cola people matrix: Muhtar Kent 2015–2018, James Quincey from 2016, Cristiano Ronaldo single 2021 spike (Euro 2020 press conference), Mark Zuckerberg single 2020 appearance (ad boycott); 2021 network shows the Georgia voting-law story cluster (Georgia/Atlanta/Delta/MLB).
46	
47	### 4. BUILD RECIPE (educational scale)
48	
49	1. **[inferred]** Assemble a news corpus with dates and, ideally, company labels — e.g., a Kaggle financial-news dataset or the project's own `data/sample/documents.jsonl`. Assumption: we substitute raw articles for NOSIBLE's de-duplicated event records; optionally cluster near-duplicate articles into "events" first (embedding + agglomerative clustering) to approximate one-record-per-event.
50	2. **[disclosed]** Run NER over every document — spaCy `en_core_web_sm/trf` yields exactly the ORG/PERSON/GPE/LOC/PRODUCT labels the post uses. Store per-document `{type: {name: count}}`.
51	3. **[inferred]** Resolve target-company mentions to a ticker. Assumption: a simple alias list (e.g., "NVIDIA"/"Nvidia Corp" → NVDA) replaces NOSIBLE's full ticker-resolution system.
52	4. **[disclosed]** Canonicalize entity surface forms: lowercase/strip-suffix merge (Apple Inc. → Apple), and per-year surname folding ("Huang" → "Jensen Huang" if that fuller form exists that year). Implement as string normalization + within-year alias map.
53	5. **[disclosed]** Bucket events by `date[:4]` and count co-mentions per (company, year, entity) exactly as the appendix `co_mentions_by_year` does — presence per event, not mention counts.
54	6. **[disclosed]** Compute per-year background counts: `target_events` (events with the company), `entity_events` (events with the entity anywhere in corpus), `total_events` (all events that year).
55	7. **[disclosed]** Score each candidate edge with `lift = (co/target_events)/(entity_events/total_events)`; keep edges well above 1.0.
56	8. **[inferred]** Normalize lift for ranking — the post says a normalized version exists but not the formula. Assumption: use `log(lift)` or lift damped by `sqrt(co)` (a minimum-support floor like `co >= 3` plus log-lift ranking is a reasonable stand-in), so rare-entity and common-entity edges are comparable.
57	9. **[disclosed]** Enforce point-in-time: never aggregate across years, no forward state; each year's graph is computed only from that year's slice. Validate by sampling edges and checking every supporting document's date lies inside the edge's year.
58	10. **[disclosed + inferred]** Build the per-year graph in `networkx`: target-company ego graph; add entity–entity edges where two entities co-occur in the same events (assumption: apply the same lift test entity-vs-entity); draw with a force-directed layout (`nx.spring_layout`), node color by NER type, node size ∝ association strength.
59	11. **[disclosed]** Build the evolution matrix in matplotlib: rows = entities, columns = years, dot size = association strength that year, dot color = change vs. prior year in the entity's share of the company's coverage (green/white/red).
60	
61	### 5. GAPS
62	
63	- The **normalized lift** formula used for ranking is never given.
64	- The **NER model/stack** is not named (no library, model size, or language handling despite "multilingual" claims).
65	- The full **canonicalization/entity-resolution algorithm** (beyond two illustrative rules) is undisclosed.
66	- How the **event deduplication** ("one record per real event") is done is not explained in this post (partially covered in the 2024 post).
67	- Edge **thresholds** (minimum lift, minimum co-count) for keeping an edge are not stated.
68	- The **entity–entity edge** criterion in the network figures ("lines join entities that also co-occur with each other") has no stated scoring rule.
69	- The embedding model, ontology facet list, and materiality-score derivation are mentioned but not specified.
70	
71	---
72	
73	## Post 2: Using Vector Search to See Signals in Company News
74	
75	**Source:** `using-vector-search-to-see-signals-in-company-news.md` (published 2024-01-21, Stuart Reid, 21 min read)
76	
77	### 1. WHAT IT IS
78	
79	An end-to-end system that curates a massive, cleaned, de-duplicated corpus of company news, embeds it with SBERT, indexes it with an ultra-fast custom **Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH)** index supporting arbitrary SQL metadata filters, and then extracts **investment signals**: weekly time series of how strongly the news matches an arbitrary natural-language query. The flagship construction is the **triplet signal** (baseline / positive / negative terms, rolling-z-scored and differenced) which works around non-discriminative embeddings ("beat" vs. "missed" estimates look alike to general encoders) and seasonal news cyclicality to produce a usable market barometer. The problem it solves: extracting Google-Trends-like, keyword-free, filterable signals from unstructured news at scale.
80	
81	### 2. ARCHITECTURE
82	
83	1. **Ingestion / ETL**: 15 OVH servers across regions; each worker runs FastAPI + Gunicorn + Nginx; tasks dispatched by Google Cloud Tasks (e.g., "go fetch news about Mastercard"); state files are compressed orjson blobs on Wasabi S3 with a data-version-control system. Fetching = (a) discover new URLs, (b) visit + parse HTML via rotating proxies; emphasis on metadata/structured SEO data — pages without SEO data often rejected.
84	2. **Company-name disambiguation** (two-stage): Stage 1 — scan story bodies for known keywords tied to overlapping entities (CEO/board names) using the **Aho-Corasick** algorithm (G-Research `ahocorasick_rs`) to get high-conviction seed stories. Stage 2 — fit probability models on contextual evidence (source domain, co-mentioned countries): "Discovery" on latimes.com → probably Warner Bros Discovery; article mentioning South Africa → ~100% Discovery (DSY). Errors handled by ensembling (the Hoya Corp / Oscar De la Hoya boxing-eye-injury blooper is the cited failure mode).
85	3. **Content cleaning**: strip inline headlines embedded mid-article (otherwise every story links to Elon Musk / spurious associations like Apple Watch ↔ ECB rate cuts).
86	4. **AI-generated-news filtering**: story-level detection deemed near-impossible; instead **blacklist domains**. Detector: distribution of a domain's snippet embeddings — AI-content farms occupy a small, densely packed region of vector space vs. legitimate outlets (ft.com, wsj.com, reuters.com); theory: static prompt + dynamic seed content constrains outputs to a small manifold. Combine embedding-spread metric with site-volume metric → good predictor. (By July 2023, AI news exceeded real news per day.)
87	5. **Deduplication**: per index build, dedupe all news and elect an **"apex" story** per duplicate cluster. Full-corpus kNN dedup would take ~11M seconds (~4 months) even at <0.20 s/query; instead shard by overlapping time windows × metadata (companies, sectors, industries, geographies, categories) and dedupe within shards → minutes.
88	6. **Indexing / semantic search**: regular full re-index of all entity news files. Query path: SQL metadata filter → candidate locations; SBERT-encode query (CPU); LSH search over matching vectors; reconstruct vectors; exact cosine on top N×M. Filters via SQL (`SELECT key FROM engine WHERE date>=... AND apex_story=True AND sector='Technology'`).
89	7. **LSH backbone**: Random Hyperplanes LSH — random vectors of dataset dimensionality; sign of dot products → bit codes → integer hashes; similarity via Hamming distance on integers (no FLOPs, cacheable, parallelizable, CPU-fast).
90	8. **Signal extraction**: filter → embed term → search all matching vectors → threshold sims → percentile-weight hits → normalize per week → weekly DataFrame; optional triplet transform (rolling z-scores, differencing).
91	9. **Validation & application**: sanity-check signals (holidays, COVID, Ukraine war, crypto, AI terms); market barometer from 5 earnings-related triplets; downstream uses: risk models (Sentio Capital), semantic advertising (Fundamental Group), sentiment-split and source-split signals via SQL filters.
92	
93	### 3. CONCRETE TECHNICAL FACTS
94	
95	- Corpus (at writing, Jan 2024): multi-terabyte; **55+ million embedded snippets, 150+ million sentences, 4+ billion words, 5+ billion GPT tokens**; growing by **300,000 snippets/day**; expanding to delisted companies; API latency target < 1 second.
96	- Infrastructure: **15 OVH servers**; FastAPI + Gunicorn + Nginx workers; Google Cloud Tasks; Wasabi S3; compressed **orjson** files; rotating proxies; SEO-metadata-gated page acceptance.
97	- Name disambiguation: Aho-Corasick via **G-Research ahocorasick_rs**; two-stage (keyword conviction set → probability models); ensemble to fix spurious probabilities. Name-collision examples: Discovery DSY (ZA), Discovery Silver DSV (CA), Discover Financial DFS (US), discoverIE DSCV (UK), Warner Bros Discovery WBD (US), Predictive Discovery PDI (AU); Hoya Corp ticker 7741 (JP).
98	- AI-news: crossover point July 2023 (more AI than real news daily); detection = per-domain embedding-distribution compactness + site volume; remedy = domain blacklist; removing AI news "improves the signals a lot".
99	- Dedup/index performance: LSH search over 55M embeddings **< 0.20 s**, "~10x faster than a flat FAISS index"; naive full dedup ≈ **11 million seconds (~4 months)**; sharded dedup = minutes; LSH throughput "**over 300 million vectors searched per second**".
100	- Example query: "Adobe Figma Merger", filter matches **3,692,137** snippets of 55M; total 0.28 s on laptop, broken down: 0.11 s SQL, 0.05 s SBERT encode (CPU), 0.09 s LSH search, 0.02 s vector reconstruction, 0.01 s cosine on top N×M.
101	- Embedding model: "**SBERT**" (sentence-transformers family; specific checkpoint not named). Encoding is CPU-only in the timing.
102	- LSH taxonomy cited: Jaccard-style (SimHash, MinHash, SuperMinHash) for order-free sets/BOW; angular-preserving (Random Hyperplanes LSH [Charikar], Voronoi LSH, Cross-Polytope LSH, Directional Feature Hashing) for embeddings. Random-hyperplane mechanics: sign(dot(v, hyperplane)) bits → grouped into integer hashes → Hamming distance ("yes yes no no no yes no yes" → 11000101 → 197).
103	- Signal code (`get_signal`), exact mechanics:
104	  - Weekly buckets keyed to Mondays (`pd.date_range(start, end, freq='W-MON')`; `index.loc2monday`).
105	  - Similarity floor: `lb = index.max_codes * 0.70` — keep only sims ≥ 70% of max code agreement (sims are in LSH code-agreement units, not raw cosine).
106	  - Percentile weighting among surviving hits: compute p20/p40/p60/p80 of sims; add **8** if sim ≥ p80, **4** if ≥ p60, **2** if ≥ p40, **1** if ≥ p20; each divided by `max_score = date2total[date] * 8` (normalizes by total filtered snippets that week × 8).
107	  - Triplet transform: for each of baseline/positive/negative series: `z = (rolling_mean(4) - rolling_mean(26)) / rolling_std(26)` (4-week SMA vs 26-week ≈ 6-month mean/SD); final signal = `(positive_z - baseline_z) - (negative_z - baseline_z)`.
108	- The five production triplets: (Quarterly Earnings / Quarterly Earnings Grew / Quarterly Earnings Fell), (Analyst Estimates / Beats Analyst Estimates / Misses Analyst Estimates), (Earnings Forecast / Increases Earnings Forecast / Decreases Earnings Forecast), (Quarterly Performance / Strong Quarterly Performance / Weak Quarterly Performance), (Earnings Guidance / Raises Earnings Guidance / Lowers Earnings Guidance). Market indicator = sum across constituent triplet signals; charted 2014-01-01 onward.
109	- Motivating observations: off-the-shelf embeddings can't separate "The company beat analyst estimates" vs "The company missed analyst estimates" (semantically opposite, geometrically near-identical); earnings-news volume is strongly seasonal (earnings seasons) and rising in absolute and proportional terms.
110	- Signal-measure definition: informativeness ≈ `G(Decisions|Signal) - G(Decisions)`.
111	- Validation signals: Christmas/Black Friday/Valentine's; COVID/SARS-CoV-2/coronavirus; Ukraine invasion/Russia-Ukraine war/Russia sanctions; Bitcoin/Ethereum/blockchain; AI/deep learning/machine learning.
112	- Named partners: Sentio Capital (risk models), Fundamental Group (semantic advertising); comparison firms: NewMark Risk (options), S3 Partners (short interest), SwaggyStocks (Reddit).
113	- Stated next steps: internet-scale data; ingest SEC filings and court cases (formal register differs from journalism); fine-tune finance-nuanced encoders bootstrapped from their own index.
114	
115	### 4. BUILD RECIPE (educational scale)
116	
117	1. **[inferred]** Corpus: use a dated financial-news dataset (or the repo's sample corpus). Assumption: a few thousand–hundred-thousand snippets stand in for 55M; skip the crawling/proxy layer entirely.
118	2. **[disclosed]** Clean: strip boilerplate/inline-headline noise (at small scale: drop lines that look like link lists; with trafilatura/readability for real HTML).
119	3. **[disclosed]** Disambiguate company mentions: build per-company keyword lists (CEO, board, products), match with Aho-Corasick (`pyahocorasick` or `ahocorasick_rs` on PyPI) for a high-conviction set; then fit a simple probabilistic model (e.g., Naive Bayes over source domain + co-mentioned GPEs) for ambiguous names; ensemble both.
120	4. **[disclosed]** AI-content filter (optional at educational scale): per-domain, embed all snippets, compute a dispersion statistic (mean pairwise cosine or trace of covariance); flag domains with low dispersion × high volume. **[inferred]** threshold choice — the post gives none; pick by inspecting the dispersion histogram.
121	5. **[disclosed]** Embed snippets with sentence-transformers (SBERT). **[inferred]** checkpoint: `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` or `all-mpnet-base-v2` — the post never names one.
122	6. **[disclosed]** Dedup: shard by (time window × metadata field), within each shard find near-duplicate clusters via cosine threshold, elect one **apex story** per cluster and flag `apex_story=True`. **[inferred]** duplicate threshold (e.g., cosine ≥ 0.9) and apex election rule (e.g., earliest or most-covered) are not stated.
123	7. **[disclosed]** Build Random Hyperplanes LSH: sample `k` random Gaussian hyperplanes matching the embedding dim; codes = `(X @ H.T > 0)` packed into ints; query = Hamming distance via XOR + popcount (numpy `bitwise_xor` + `bit_count`, or use FAISS `IndexLSH` for the lesson). **[inferred]** number of bits/tables not disclosed; 64–256 bits works at small scale.
124	8. **[disclosed]** Metadata filtering: store snippet metadata (date, sector, company, apex_story, sentiment, source) in a queryable table (Polars/DuckDB/SQLite) and resolve SQL filters to row locations before the vector search — filter-then-search, not post-filter.
125	9. **[disclosed]** Signal extraction: port `get_signal` almost verbatim — weekly Monday buckets; search the filtered set for each term; drop hits below 70% of max code score; weight by within-run percentile (8/4/2/1 at p80/p60/p40/p20); divide by `weekly_count * 8`.
126	10. **[disclosed]** Triplet signals: implement the exact z-score construction (4-week SMA, 26-week rolling mean/SD, `(pos_z − base_z) − (neg_z − base_z)`) with pandas; use the five published earnings triplets; sum for the barometer.
127	11. **[disclosed]** Validate: run the seasonal/holiday and event-driven queries (COVID, Ukraine, crypto, AI) and eyeball that spikes land on known dates.
128	
129	### 5. GAPS
130	
131	- The **exact SBERT checkpoint**, embedding dimensionality, and snippet-chunking scheme are never disclosed.
132	- LSH engineering details withheld: number of hyperplanes/bits, tables, multi-probe strategy, "more advanced LSH algorithms" explicitly deferred to future posts; how 300M vectors/s is reached (SIMD/layout) unstated.
133	- **Dedup thresholds** and the **apex-story election rule** are not given; shard window sizes/overlaps unstated.
134	- The AI-news detector's **actual metric and thresholds** ("More on this in later blogs") are withheld.
135	- Stage-2 disambiguation **probability-model form** and the ensembling scheme are not specified.
136	- Sentiment model, the SQL engine internals (the "engine" table), and evaluation results of the market barometer (promised follow-up) are not disclosed.
137	
138	---
139	
140	## Post 3: Two Tricks for Turning Sentence Embeddings into Clean Features ("The Contrastive Geometry of Risk")
141	
142	**Source:** `the-contrastive-geometry-of-risk.md` (published 2026-06-18, Stuart Reid, 14 min read)
143	
144	### 1. WHAT IT IS
145	
146	A training-free, LLM-free method for classifying news events along custom dimensions using only frozen sentence embeddings and elementary geometry. Two "tricks": (A) a **multiclass relevance score** — hand-written reference-sentence sets per bucket, cosine similarities gated through a tanh band and aggregated with a cubic power mean, argmax over buckets (demonstrated on geographic scale: local/national/global); (B) a **binary signed contrast** — two mirror-image reference sets whose common mode is subtracted out ("common-mode neutralization"), then the score is mean-cosine-to-set-A minus mean-cosine-to-set-B (demonstrated on idiosyncratic vs. systemic risk). It solves labeling at corpus scale where an LLM is slow, expensive, non-deterministic, unauditable, and — critically for backtests — leaks **foreknowledge bias**; a frozen embedding with a September 2021 cutoff cannot know how post-2021 events turned out.
147	
148	### 2. ARCHITECTURE
149	
150	The full 10-step pipeline as disclosed (one event carried end-to-end; running input: "Central banks across every major economy warn that a synchronized financial shock is freezing credit and driving stock markets lower worldwide." — expected global + systemic):
151	
152	1. Author reference texts for each geographic bucket — 20 sentences per bucket (local/national/global), near mirror images: same declarative frames repeated across sets, only the scale phrase varies (topic and style held constant so they cancel; only geographic scale separates the sets).
153	2. Embed all references with OpenAI `text-embedding-3-large` (3,072-dim, frozen, Sept-2021 knowledge cutoff — chosen for backtest safety).
154	3. Cosine-score the input sentence against all 60 references (raw values noisy, buckets overlap).
155	4. **Tanh gate**: pass cosines through a tanh band from **0.25 to 0.50** — below collapses toward 0, above saturates toward 1 (kills the ~0.3 "same register" background floor).
156	5. **Cubic power mean (p=3)** per bucket over the gated cosines → one score per bucket; leans toward the strongest matches. Argmax picks the bucket. A **dead-zone floor** returns a clean "none" if no bucket clears it (off-topic events left unassigned rather than forced).
157	6. Author mirror texts for the binary axis — 20 pairs, identical sentences except the words flipping single-company ↔ whole-market; topics deliberately *vary across pairs* so averaging cancels topic and leaves only the flip. (These are the real production pairs.)
158	7. Embed both mirror sets the same way; raw 2-D projection shows the sets overlap completely (shared financial register dominates; raw cosine cannot separate them).
159	8. **Common-mode neutralization**: subtract the mean of all reference vectors from each vector, renormalize. The shared coordinate drops from **+0.71 to +0.005**; sets separate cleanly along the contrast direction.
160	9. **Signed cosine contrast**: score = mean cosine to neutralized idiosyncratic set − mean cosine to neutralized systemic set. Positive → idiosyncratic (one company); negative → systemic (whole market). Running input scores **−0.068** (systemic — correct).
161	10. **Fusion**: the two reads are independent → place each event on a 2-D plane (geographic scale × scope). The running input lands in the global/systemic corner.
162	
163	Verification stage: 18 sentences (3 geographies × 2 scopes × 3 samples; national/global cases pulled from the NOSIBLE World leaderboard, local cases authored because the leaderboard has nothing at town scale), hand-labeled, scored through the pipeline, and benchmarked head-to-head against `gemini-2.5-flash` at temperature 0.
164	
165	### 3. CONCRETE TECHNICAL FACTS
166	
167	- Embedding model: OpenAI **`text-embedding-3-large`**, **3,072 dimensions**, frozen, **September 2021 knowledge cutoff** — chosen to eliminate foreknowledge bias in backtests.
168	- Reference-set sizes: **20 sentences per bucket**, 3 geographic buckets = 60 references; **20 mirror pairs** for the binary axis (all sentences printed verbatim in the post — reusable as-is).
169	- Reference-authoring rules: multiclass sets = same declarative frame across sets, only the scale phrase varies (constant topic/style cancels); mirror sets = identical sentence up to the single-company↔whole-market flip, with topics varied *across* pairs so averaging cancels topic.
170	- Background-noise fact: two unrelated sentences in the same clipped declarative register score ≈ **0.3** cosine.
171	- **Tanh gate band: 0.25 → 0.50** (below → 0, above → 1). Exact functional form not printed; described as "a tanh gate over the cosines, with a band from 0.25 to 0.50".
172	- **Aggregation: cubic power mean, p = 3** (i.e., `(mean(x³))^(1/3)` over a bucket's gated cosines).
173	- Worked bucket scores for the running input: **local 0.315, national 0.417, global 0.739** → argmax global.
174	- **Dead-zone floor** for "none" assignment exists (value not given).
175	- Neutralization effect (exact): shared coordinate **+0.71 → +0.005** after subtracting the mean reference vector and renormalizing.
176	- Signed contrast score of the running input: **−0.068** (systemic side).
177	- Verification scope scores are tabulated per sentence (range roughly −0.059 to +0.065; e.g., Tesla warning +0.043, SpaceX +0.028, Samsung strike −0.005, USPS −0.016, Tongaat Hulett +0.022, TG Jones +0.038).
178	- Accuracy: geometry — **geography 16/18, scope 15/18, both axes 13/18**; `gemini-2.5-flash` (temperature 0) — **identical: 16/18, 15/18, 13/18** ("a dead heat on all three"); both fail the same hard cases (Samsung supply-chain strike and USPS read systemic); Gemini also calls Tongaat Hulett systemic and puts Tesla/SpaceX in "national".
179	- Geometry's misses: Canada macro warning tips global (should be national); TG Jones reads local (should be national); mill-town closure reads idiosyncratic (should be systemic); USPS reads systemic (labeled idiosyncratic); Samsung reads systemic (labeled idiosyncratic).
180	- Characteristic failure mode: single companies whose trouble bleeds into a whole sector/market (scope), and company scale vs. geographic reach confusion (geography).
181	- Five stated advantages over LLM labeling: deterministic/reproducible; defensible (every output is a cosine, a mean, or a subtraction — re-derivable by hand, explainable to a regulator); cheap/fast at scale (one embedding per doc + linear algebra vs. one LLM call per doc per question); no training and no labelled data (writing reference sentences is the entire setup); no foreknowledge bias.
182	- Provenance notes: every figure generated from real `text-embedding-3-large` vectors; geographic reference texts authored for the post; verification set mixes authored local cases with real NOSIBLE World leaderboard warnings; systemic/idiosyncratic mirror sets "taken straight from production".
183	
184	### 4. BUILD RECIPE (educational scale)
185	
186	1. **[disclosed]** Copy the reference sets — both 20×3 geographic sets and the 20 mirror pairs are printed in full in the post; or author your own dimension following the disclosed rules (constant frame, vary only the target attribute; for binary axes, mirror pairs with varied topics).
187	2. **[disclosed / inferred]** Embed with a frozen model. Post uses OpenAI `text-embedding-3-large` (3,072-d). Local substitute: sentence-transformers (e.g., `all-mpnet-base-v2` or `BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5`) — assumption: any frozen, reasonably strong sentence encoder preserves the geometry; the gate band may need retuning since the ~0.3 background floor is model-specific.
188	3. **[disclosed]** L2-normalize; compute cosine of the input against all 60 geo references (numpy dot products).
189	4. **[disclosed + inferred]** Tanh gate on band [0.25, 0.50]. The band is disclosed; the exact parameterization is not. Assumption: `gated = 0.5 * (1 + tanh(k * (cos − c)))` with center `c = 0.375` (band midpoint) and steepness `k` chosen so 0.25 → ≈0 and 0.50 → ≈1 (k ≈ 8–12).
190	5. **[disclosed]** Per-bucket cubic mean: `score_b = (mean(gated_b ** 3)) ** (1/3)`; predict `argmax`; **[inferred]** dead-zone: return "none" if max score < ~0.2–0.3 (post confirms the floor exists, not its value).
191	6. **[disclosed]** For the binary axis: embed the 40 mirror sentences; compute `mu = mean(all 40 vectors)`; neutralize each: `v' = normalize(v − mu)`.
192	7. **[disclosed + inferred]** Score input `x`: `contrast = mean(cos(x', idio_set')) − mean(cos(x', sys_set'))`; sign gives the label. **[inferred]** whether the input is also neutralized with the same `mu` is not stated; neutralizing it (x' = normalize(x − mu)) is the natural reading and is assumed here.
193	8. **[disclosed]** Fuse: scatter events on (geo-bucket, signed-contrast) axes.
194	9. **[disclosed]** Verify: build an ~18-sentence hand-labeled set spanning all cells of the grid (include deliberately hard cases: big company with market-wide spillover); report per-axis and joint accuracy; optionally benchmark against an LLM at temperature 0 for the comparison lesson.
195	10. **[inferred]** Reproduce the diagnostic plots — strip plot of raw vs. gated cosines, and 2-D projection of mirror sets before/after neutralization — with matplotlib/scikit-learn; assumption: PCA is the projection (the post just says "project ... down to two dimensions").
196	
197	### 5. GAPS
198	
199	- **Exact tanh-gate formula** (center, steepness, scaling) — only the 0.25–0.50 band is given.
200	- **Dead-zone floor value** for the "none" class.
201	- Whether the **input vector is neutralized** with the reference mean before the signed contrast (strongly implied, not stated); whether contrast uses per-set mean vectors vs. mean-of-cosines is compressed into one sentence ("mean cosine to the neutralized ... set").
202	- The **2-D projection method** in the figures (PCA vs. other) is unstated.
203	- How the tricks are wired into **production NOSIBLE World** (which axes ship, at what thresholds, how scores are stored/queried) — only "the mirror sets are from production" is admitted.
204	- The **geographic reference sets are authored "for this post"** — production geographic sets (if any) are withheld.
205	- No ablations: sensitivity to reference-set size (why 20?), gate band, or power-mean exponent is not reported.
206	
207	---
208	
209	## Cross-post synthesis (for the build guide)
210	
211	The three posts describe one coherent stack, disclosed at three layers:
212	
213	1. The 2024 vector-search post is the **substrate** — cleaned, disambiguated, deduped, SBERT-embedded, LSH-indexed, SQL-filterable news snippets and the query→weekly-signal machinery.
214	2. The contrastive-geometry post is the **enrichment layer** — cheap, frozen-embedding, backtest-safe categorical/axis features stamped onto every event.
215	3. The knowledge-graph post is the **structural layer** — NER + yearly lift over the same event records, producing point-in-time entity graphs.
216	
217	Common thread: every technique is deliberately deterministic, auditable, and free of lookahead/foreknowledge bias (year-bucketed lift; frozen Sept-2021 encoder; date-stamped edges). That is the architectural signature an educational replica should preserve: **date-partition everything, freeze the encoder, and make every score re-derivable from counts, cosines, means, and subtractions.**

# Clean-Room Reverse-Engineering Notes: Three NOSIBLE Blog Posts

Educational replica notes for a cybernaut_mini-style project. Sources are the three archived posts under `/Users/neelanpather/dev/cybernaut_mini/docs/blog-archive/`.

---

## Post 1: Point-in-Time Knowledge Graphs over Named Entities with NOSIBLE World

**Source:** `point-in-time-knowledge-graphs-over-named-entities.md` (published 2026-07-16, "NOSIBLE Research", 8 min read)

### 1. WHAT IT IS

A pipeline that builds **point-in-time knowledge graphs** over named entities extracted from a de-duplicated global news-event database (NOSIBLE World). Nodes are NER entities (companies, people, products, places); edges are inferred from statistical co-mention **lift** within a single year's news; every edge is date-bucketed so a graph "as of 2018" contains only information knowable in 2018. The problem it solves is **lookahead bias** in backtesting: conventional knowledge graphs accumulate future facts into past views (e.g., a 2007 model "knowing" the iPhone will succeed), which invalidates historical evaluation. The point-in-time construction makes the graph safe to backtest by construction.

### 2. ARCHITECTURE

Ordered data flow as disclosed:

1. **Event database (NOSIBLE World)** — the article stream is collapsed into *one record per real event* (regardless of how many outlets covered it). Each record carries: date, NER entities (with per-name mention counts, grouped by type), resolved company tickers (EODHD format, plus ISIN/LEI/FIGI), coverage counts (total_coverage, total_netlocs = distinct publishers), sentiment + materiality signals, a semantic embedding of the event's meaning, a 20-facet ontology (GICS, IPTC, NOSIBLE event types among them), and per-publisher provenance.
2. **NER layer** — NER runs over every event; many entity types recorded; the post uses five: `ORG`, `PERSON`, `GPE`, `LOC` (places), `PRODUCT`.
3. **Event selection** — scan every daily slice for the study window (2015 → mid-2026), pull events whose resolved tickers include the target company.
4. **Entity canonicalization** — surface forms collapsed ("Apple", "Apple Inc.", "apple" → one node); a lone surname folds into the fuller name kept that year.
5. **Yearly co-mention counting** — bucket every event by its document date's year; per (company, year, entity) count events co-mentioning both. No cumulative or forward-looking state — point-in-time by construction.
6. **Edge scoring by lift** — compare the co-mention rate against the entity's background rate in the same year's whole corpus. A normalized version of lift is used for ranking so a strong link on a rare product ranks alongside one on a common name.
7. **Edge filtering** — ubiquitous entities (e.g., "United States") get lift ≈ 1.0 and fall away; high-lift edges kept.
8. **Validation** — sample edges at random, pull the underlying source documents, verify all fall inside the edge's year.
9. **Visualization** — (a) per-year force-directed network: nodes = entities co-mentioned with the target; edges join entities that also co-occur *with each other* so related nodes cluster; node color = category, node size = association strength. (b) Evolution matrix (entity × year): dot size = that year's association strength; dot color = year-over-year change in the entity's share of the company's coverage (green grew / white flat / red shrank).

### 3. CONCRETE TECHNICAL FACTS

## Post 2: Using Vector Search to See Signals in Company News

**Source:** `using-vector-search-to-see-signals-in-company-news.md` (published 2024-01-21, Stuart Reid, 21 min read)

### 1. WHAT IT IS

An end-to-end system that curates a massive, cleaned, de-duplicated corpus of company news, embeds it with SBERT, indexes it with an ultra-fast custom **Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH)** index supporting arbitrary SQL metadata filters, and then extracts **investment signals**: weekly time series of how strongly the news matches an arbitrary natural-language query. The flagship construction is the **triplet signal** (baseline / positive / negative terms, rolling-z-scored and differenced) which works around non-discriminative embeddings ("beat" vs. "missed" estimates look alike to general encoders) and seasonal news cyclicality to produce a usable market barometer. The problem it solves: extracting Google-Trends-like, keyword-free, filterable signals from unstructured news at scale.

### 2. ARCHITECTURE

1. **Ingestion / ETL**: 15 OVH servers across regions; each worker runs FastAPI + Gunicorn + Nginx; tasks dispatched by Google Cloud Tasks (e.g., "go fetch news about Mastercard"); state files are compressed orjson blobs on Wasabi S3 with a data-version-control system. Fetching = (a) discover new URLs, (b) visit + parse HTML via rotating proxies; emphasis on metadata/structured SEO data — pages without SEO data often rejected.
2. **Company-name disambiguation** (two-stage): Stage 1 — scan story bodies for known keywords tied to overlapping entities (CEO/board names) using the **Aho-Corasick** algorithm (G-Research `ahocorasick_rs`) to get high-conviction seed stories. Stage 2 — fit probability models on contextual evidence (source domain, co-mentioned countries): "Discovery" on latimes.com → probably Warner Bros Discovery; article mentioning South Africa → ~100% Discovery (DSY). Errors handled by ensembling (the Hoya Corp / Oscar De la Hoya boxing-eye-injury blooper is the cited failure mode).
3. **Content cleaning**: strip inline headlines embedded mid-article (otherwise every story links to Elon Musk / spurious associations like Apple Watch ↔ ECB rate cuts).
4. **AI-generated-news filtering**: story-level detection deemed near-impossible; instead **blacklist domains**. Detector: distribution of a domain's snippet embeddings — AI-content farms occupy a small, densely packed region of vector space vs. legitimate outlets (ft.com, wsj.com, reuters.com); theory: static prompt + dynamic seed content constrains outputs to a small manifold. Combine embedding-spread metric with site-volume metric → good predictor. (By July 2023, AI news exceeded real news per day.)
5. **Deduplication**: per index build, dedupe all news and elect an **"apex" story** per duplicate cluster. Full-corpus kNN dedup would take ~11M seconds (~4 months) even at <0.20 s/query; instead shard by overlapping time windows × metadata (companies, sectors, industries, geographies, categories) and dedupe within shards → minutes.
6. **Indexing / semantic search**: regular full re-index of all entity news files. Query path: SQL metadata filter → candidate locations; SBERT-encode query (CPU); LSH search over matching vectors; reconstruct vectors; exact cosine on top N×M. Filters via SQL (`SELECT key FROM engine WHERE date>=... AND apex_story=True AND sector='Technology'`).
7. **LSH backbone**: Random Hyperplanes LSH — random vectors of dataset dimensionality; sign of dot products → bit codes → integer hashes; similarity via Hamming distance on integers (no FLOPs, cacheable, parallelizable, CPU-fast).
8. **Signal extraction**: filter → embed term → search all matching vectors → threshold sims → percentile-weight hits → normalize per week → weekly DataFrame; optional triplet transform (rolling z-scores, differencing).
9. **Validation & application**: sanity-check signals (holidays, COVID, Ukraine war, crypto, AI terms); market barometer from 5 earnings-related triplets; downstream uses: risk models (Sentio Capital), semantic advertising (Fundamental Group), sentiment-split and source-split signals via SQL filters.

### 3. CONCRETE TECHNICAL FACTS

- Corpus (at writing, Jan 2024): multi-terabyte; **55+ million embedded snippets, 150+ million sentences, 4+ billion words, 5+ billion GPT tokens**; growing by **300,000 snippets/day**; expanding to delisted companies; API latency target < 1 second.
- Infrastructure: **15 OVH servers**; FastAPI + Gunicorn + Nginx workers; Google Cloud Tasks; Wasabi S3; compressed **orjson** files; rotating proxies; SEO-metadata-gated page acceptance.
- Name disambiguation: Aho-Corasick via **G-Research ahocorasick_rs**; two-stage (keyword conviction set → probability models); ensemble to fix spurious probabilities. Name-collision examples: Discovery DSY (ZA), Discovery Silver DSV (CA), Discover Financial DFS (US), discoverIE DSCV (UK), Warner Bros Discovery WBD (US), Predictive Discovery PDI (AU); Hoya Corp ticker 7741 (JP).
- AI-news: crossover point July 2023 (more AI than real news daily); detection = per-domain embedding-distribution compactness + site volume; remedy = domain blacklist; removing AI news "improves the signals a lot".
- Dedup/index performance: LSH search over 55M embeddings **< 0.20 s**, "~10x faster than a flat FAISS index"; naive full dedup ≈ **11 million seconds (~4 months)**; sharded dedup = minutes; LSH throughput "**over 300 million vectors searched per second**".
- Example query: "Adobe Figma Merger", filter matches **3,692,137** snippets of 55M; total 0.28 s on laptop, broken down: 0.11 s SQL, 0.05 s SBERT encode (CPU), 0.09 s LSH search, 0.02 s vector reconstruction, 0.01 s cosine on top N×M.
- Embedding model: "**SBERT**" (sentence-transformers family; specific checkpoint not named). Encoding is CPU-only in the timing.
- LSH taxonomy cited: Jaccard-style (SimHash, MinHash, SuperMinHash) for order-free sets/BOW; angular-preserving (Random Hyperplanes LSH [Charikar], Voronoi LSH, Cross-Polytope LSH, Directional Feature Hashing) for embeddings. Random-hyperplane mechanics: sign(dot(v, hyperplane)) bits → grouped into integer hashes → Hamming distance ("yes yes no no no yes no yes" → 11000101 → 197).
- Signal code (`get_signal`), exact mechanics:
  - Weekly buckets keyed to Mondays (`pd.date_range(start, end, freq='W-MON')`; `index.loc2monday`).
  - Similarity floor: `lb = index.max_codes * 0.70` — keep only sims ≥ 70% of max code agreement (sims are in LSH code-agreement units, not raw cosine).
  - Percentile weighting among surviving hits: compute p20/p40/p60/p80 of sims; add **8** if sim ≥ p80, **4** if ≥ p60, **2** if ≥ p40, **1** if ≥ p20; each divided by `max_score = date2total[date] * 8` (normalizes by total filtered snippets that week × 8).
  - Triplet transform: for each of baseline/positive/negative series: `z = (rolling_mean(4) - rolling_mean(26)) / rolling_std(26)` (4-week SMA vs 26-week ≈ 6-month mean/SD); final signal = `(positive_z - baseline_z) - (negative_z - baseline_z)`.
- The five production triplets: (Quarterly Earnings / Quarterly Earnings Grew / Quarterly Earnings Fell), (Analyst Estimates / Beats Analyst Estimates / Misses Analyst Estimates), (Earnings Forecast / Increases Earnings Forecast / Decreases Earnings Forecast), (Quarterly Performance / Strong Quarterly Performance / Weak Quarterly Performance), (Earnings Guidance / Raises Earnings Guidance / Lowers Earnings Guidance). Market indicator = sum across constituent triplet signals; charted 2014-01-01 onward.
- Motivating observations: off-the-shelf embeddings can't separate "The company beat analyst estimates" vs "The company missed analyst estimates" (semantically opposite, geometrically near-identical); earnings-news volume is strongly seasonal (earnings seasons) and rising in absolute and proportional terms.
- Signal-measure definition: informativeness ≈ `G(Decisions|Signal) - G(Decisions)`.
- Validation signals: Christmas/Black Friday/Valentine's; COVID/SARS-CoV-2/coronavirus; Ukraine invasion/Russia-Ukraine war/Russia sanctions; Bitcoin/Ethereum/blockchain; AI/deep learning/machine learning.
- Named partners: Sentio Capital (risk models), Fundamental Group (semantic advertising); comparison firms: NewMark Risk (options), S3 Partners (short interest), SwaggyStocks (Reddit).
- Stated next steps: internet-scale data; ingest SEC filings and court cases (formal register differs from journalism); fine-tune finance-nuanced encoders bootstrapped from their own index.

## Post 3: Two Tricks for Turning Sentence Embeddings into Clean Features ("The Contrastive Geometry of Risk")

**Source:** `the-contrastive-geometry-of-risk.md` (published 2026-06-18, Stuart Reid, 14 min read)

### 1. WHAT IT IS

A training-free, LLM-free method for classifying news events along custom dimensions using only frozen sentence embeddings and elementary geometry. Two "tricks": (A) a **multiclass relevance score** — hand-written reference-sentence sets per bucket, cosine similarities gated through a tanh band and aggregated with a cubic power mean, argmax over buckets (demonstrated on geographic scale: local/national/global); (B) a **binary signed contrast** — two mirror-image reference sets whose common mode is subtracted out ("common-mode neutralization"), then the score is mean-cosine-to-set-A minus mean-cosine-to-set-B (demonstrated on idiosyncratic vs. systemic risk). It solves labeling at corpus scale where an LLM is slow, expensive, non-deterministic, unauditable, and — critically for backtests — leaks **foreknowledge bias**; a frozen embedding with a September 2021 cutoff cannot know how post-2021 events turned out.

### 2. ARCHITECTURE

The full 10-step pipeline as disclosed (one event carried end-to-end; running input: "Central banks across every major economy warn that a synchronized financial shock is freezing credit and driving stock markets lower worldwide." — expected global + systemic):

1. Author reference texts for each geographic bucket — 20 sentences per bucket (local/national/global), near mirror images: same declarative frames repeated across sets, only the scale phrase varies (topic and style held constant so they cancel; only geographic scale separates the sets).
2. Embed all references with OpenAI `text-embedding-3-large` (3,072-dim, frozen, Sept-2021 knowledge cutoff — chosen for backtest safety).
3. Cosine-score the input sentence against all 60 references (raw values noisy, buckets overlap).
4. **Tanh gate**: pass cosines through a tanh band from **0.25 to 0.50** — below collapses toward 0, above saturates toward 1 (kills the ~0.3 "same register" background floor).
5. **Cubic power mean (p=3)** per bucket over the gated cosines → one score per bucket; leans toward the strongest matches. Argmax picks the bucket. A **dead-zone floor** returns a clean "none" if no bucket clears it (off-topic events left unassigned rather than forced).
6. Author mirror texts for the binary axis — 20 pairs, identical sentences except the words flipping single-company ↔ whole-market; topics deliberately *vary across pairs* so averaging cancels topic and leaves only the flip. (These are the real production pairs.)
7. Embed both mirror sets the same way; raw 2-D projection shows the sets overlap completely (shared financial register dominates; raw cosine cannot separate them).
8. **Common-mode neutralization**: subtract the mean of all reference vectors from each vector, renormalize. The shared coordinate drops from **+0.71 to +0.005**; sets separate cleanly along the contrast direction.
9. **Signed cosine contrast**: score = mean cosine to neutralized idiosyncratic set − mean cosine to neutralized systemic set. Positive → idiosyncratic (one company); negative → systemic (whole market). Running input scores **−0.068** (systemic — correct).
10. **Fusion**: the two reads are independent → place each event on a 2-D plane (geographic scale × scope). The running input lands in the global/systemic corner.

Verification stage: 18 sentences (3 geographies × 2 scopes × 3 samples; national/global cases pulled from the NOSIBLE World leaderboard, local cases authored because the leaderboard has nothing at town scale), hand-labeled, scored through the pipeline, and benchmarked head-to-head against `gemini-2.5-flash` at temperature 0.

### 3. CONCRETE TECHNICAL FACTS

- Embedding model: OpenAI **`text-embedding-3-large`**, **3,072 dimensions**, frozen, **September 2021 knowledge cutoff** — chosen to eliminate foreknowledge bias in backtests.
- Reference-set sizes: **20 sentences per bucket**, 3 geographic buckets = 60 references; **20 mirror pairs** for the binary axis (all sentences printed verbatim in the post — reusable as-is).
- Reference-authoring rules: multiclass sets = same declarative frame across sets, only the scale phrase varies (constant topic/style cancels); mirror sets = identical sentence up to the single-company↔whole-market flip, with topics varied *across* pairs so averaging cancels topic.
- Background-noise fact: two unrelated sentences in the same clipped declarative register score ≈ **0.3** cosine.
- **Tanh gate band: 0.25 → 0.50** (below → 0, above → 1). Exact functional form not printed; described as "a tanh gate over the cosines, with a band from 0.25 to 0.50".
- **Aggregation: cubic power mean, p = 3** (i.e., `(mean(x³))^(1/3)` over a bucket's gated cosines).
- Worked bucket scores for the running input: **local 0.315, national 0.417, global 0.739** → argmax global.
- **Dead-zone floor** for "none" assignment exists (value not given).
- Neutralization effect (exact): shared coordinate **+0.71 → +0.005** after subtracting the mean reference vector and renormalizing.
- Signed contrast score of the running input: **−0.068** (systemic side).
- Verification scope scores are tabulated per sentence (range roughly −0.059 to +0.065; e.g., Tesla warning +0.043, SpaceX +0.028, Samsung strike −0.005, USPS −0.016, Tongaat Hulett +0.022, TG Jones +0.038).
- Accuracy: geometry — **geography 16/18, scope 15/18, both axes 13/18**; `gemini-2.5-flash` (temperature 0) — **identical: 16/18, 15/18, 13/18** ("a dead heat on all three"); both fail the same hard cases (Samsung supply-chain strike and USPS read systemic); Gemini also calls Tongaat Hulett systemic and puts Tesla/SpaceX in "national".
- Geometry's misses: Canada macro warning tips global (should be national); TG Jones reads local (should be national); mill-town closure reads idiosyncratic (should be systemic); USPS reads systemic (labeled idiosyncratic); Samsung reads systemic (labeled idiosyncratic).
- Characteristic failure mode: single companies whose trouble bleeds into a whole sector/market (scope), and company scale vs. geographic reach confusion (geography).
- Five stated advantages over LLM labeling: deterministic/reproducible; defensible (every output is a cosine, a mean, or a subtraction — re-derivable by hand, explainable to a regulator); cheap/fast at scale (one embedding per doc + linear algebra vs. one LLM call per doc per question); no training and no labelled data (writing reference sentences is the entire setup); no foreknowledge bias.
- Provenance notes: every figure generated from real `text-embedding-3-large` vectors; geographic reference texts authored for the post; verification set mixes authored local cases with real NOSIBLE World leaderboard warnings; systemic/idiosyncratic mirror sets "taken straight from production".

## Cross-post synthesis (for the build guide)

The three posts describe one coherent stack, disclosed at three layers:

1. The 2024 vector-search post is the **substrate** — cleaned, disambiguated, deduped, SBERT-embedded, LSH-indexed, SQL-filterable news snippets and the query→weekly-signal machinery.
2. The contrastive-geometry post is the **enrichment layer** — cheap, frozen-embedding, backtest-safe categorical/axis features stamped onto every event.
3. The knowledge-graph post is the **structural layer** — NER + yearly lift over the same event records, producing point-in-time entity graphs.

Common thread: every technique is deliberately deterministic, auditable, and free of lookahead/foreknowledge bias (year-bucketed lift; frozen Sept-2021 encoder; date-stamped edges). That is the architectural signature an educational replica should preserve: **date-partition everything, freeze the encoder, and make every score re-derivable from counts, cosines, means, and subtractions.**

1	# NOSIBLE Blog Archive: Clean-Room Reverse-Engineering Notes
2	
3	Educational replica notes covering three posts from the NOSIBLE technical blog, in chronological order (the 2024 posts form a two-part series that the 2025 post supersedes).

6	
7	## Post 1: "News Sentiment Showdown: Who Checks Vibes Best?" (2024-01-28)
8	
9	Source: `/Users/neelanpather/dev/cybernaut_mini/docs/blog-archive/news-sentiment-showdown-who-checks-vibes-best.md` — Author: Stuart Reid
10	
11	### 1. WHAT IT IS
12	
13	A benchmark study answering "how can financial-news sentiment be quantified?" It compares 12+ sentiment classifiers — spanning lexicon models (TextBlob, VADER), pre-LLM transformers (Flair, FinBERT, FinBERT-Tone, SigmaFSA), and cloud LLMs (GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-4, GPT-4-Turbo, PaLM-2 Bison/Unicorn, Gemini-Pro) — against 250 hand-labeled news stories and a representative 10,368-story corpus subset. The problem it solves: identifying which model best matches human sentiment judgment on real financial news, and quantifying the cost of using cloud LLMs at corpus scale (10M stories). It sets up the distillation post that follows.
14	
15	### 2. ARCHITECTURE
16	
17	1. **Corpus filtering** — SQL query over the NOSIBLE news index ("engine" table) run in a nested for-loop over (year × category × industry), selecting the top stories by `media_coverage` per intersection.
18	2. **Dataset carving** — three tiers: `nosible-news-small` (10,368 records; biggest 1 story per intersection), `nosible-news-medium` (22,422; biggest 3), `nosible-news-large` (43,324; biggest 5). "Biggest" = most widely covered by independent publishers simultaneously (proxy for impact/realness).
19	3. **Hand-labeling** — 250 randomly chosen stories labeled by humans (Positive/Neutral/Negative) as ground truth.
20	4. **Model inference** — every model labels the stories; LLMs all receive the identical few-shot prompt with zero modifications; input text is headline + description.
21	5. **Evaluation** — pairwise agreement matrices: (a) all models vs. human labels on the 250 hand-labeled set (rows/cols ordered by human agreement), (b) all models vs. each other on the 10,368-story small set (ordered by agreement with Text-Bison, the best on that set).
22	6. **Cost analysis** — average cost per story labeled per cloud LLM, extrapolated to 10M stories.
23	
24	### 3. CONCRETE TECHNICAL FACTS
25	
26	**Dataset construction:**
27	- Representation constraints: news from all years 2014–2023, all 30 Nosible news categories, all 145 industries.
28	- Quality filters (verbatim from SQL): `source_language_rank>=0.50`, `source_variance_rank>=0.50`, `accepted=true`, `apex_story=true`, `source_is_banned=false`, `media_coverage>=3`, `title_num_words>=5 AND <=25`, `description_num_words>=10 AND <=50`, `ORDER BY media_coverage DESC LIMIT 10` per (year, category, industry) cell.
29	- Note: prose says "description between 5 and 50 words" but the SQL says `>=10` — SQL is authoritative.
30	- Dataset fields: Headline, Description (lede/SEO description), Category, Company, Sector (GICS), Industry (GICS), Continent, Country.
31	- 250 hand-labeled stories chosen at random; authors admit internal disagreement on several labels.
32	
33	**Models evaluated (with thresholds):**
34	- Random baseline: −1/0/+1 with equal probability (useful for post-test probabilities).
35	- TextBlob [2013]: lexicon polarity, thresholds 0.15 / 0.30 / 0.45.
36	- VADER [2014]: lexicon+rules compound score, 3 thresholds (results reference VADER-0.10, -0.20, -0.30).
37	- Flair [2019]: distilBERT-based, binary POS/NEG; converted to 3-class by accepting the top label only if probability crossed a confidence threshold — tested at 70%, 80%, 90%.
38	- FinBERT [2019]: `ProsusAI/finbert` on Hugging Face.
39	- SigmaFSA [2022]: `Sigma/financial-sentiment-analysis` on Hugging Face (appears to be fine-tuned Financial BERT, not FinBERT).
40	- FinBERT-Tone [2023]: `yiyanghkust/finbert-tone` on Hugging Face.
41	- GPT-3.5-Turbo [2022]: accessed via LangChain.
42	- Text-Bison [2023]: PaLM 2, via Google Cloud Platform, default hyperparameters.
43	- Text-Unicorn [2023]: largest PaLM 2 model, via GCP, default hyperparameters.
44	- GPT-4 [2023]: via OpenAI API.
45	- GPT-4-Turbo [2023]: specifically `gpt-4-1106-preview`.
46	- Gemini-Pro [2023]: via Google Cloud (nano and ultra unavailable to them).
47	
48	**Prompt (few-shot, identical for all LLMs):** system framing "You are a sentiment classification AI"; constrained to reply only POS/NEU/NEG; "When you are unsure of the sentiment, you MUST reply with NEU"; exactly 9 few-shot examples (3 POS, 3 NEU, 3 NEG, covering product demand, market/jobs numbers, and FDA/pharma scenarios); ends with `Story: {story}\nReply:`. Full prompt text is disclosed verbatim in the post.
49	
50	**Results (agreement with human labels):**
51	- Text-Unicorn (PaLM-2): 84% — 1st place.
52	- GPT-4: 74% — 2nd place; 8% higher than GPT-4-Turbo (so GPT-4-Turbo ≈ 66%).
53	- FinBERT: ~69% ("better off using FinBERT than GPT-3.5"; agrees with Unicorn the same amount as GPT-3.5).
54	- FinBERT-Tone: agreed with Unicorn only 53% vs FinBERT's 69% — a regression.
55	- VADER (0.10 threshold): agreed with Unicorn 56% of the time; TextBlob "very nearly random."
56	- Gemini-Pro beat Bison (same pricing model; they'd choose Gemini-Pro). Speculation that Gemini-Ultra would beat Unicorn.
57	- Flair, SigmaFSA, FinBERT-Tone did not outperform VADER despite higher compute cost — attributed to overfitting to their training domains.
58	
59	**Cost/speed:**
60	- GPT-4 average cost per story: $0.00983; GPT-4-Turbo: $0.00329 (GPT-4-Turbo 2.98× cheaper).
61	- VADER is 339× faster than FinBERT — "may still have a place in real-time trading environments."
62	- 10M-story extrapolation shown in bar chart (the $92,000 GPT-4 total is stated in the follow-up post).
63	- The NOSIBLE corpus already exceeded 10M documents at time of writing.
64	
65	**Other labeling tasks named (pattern generalizes):** Sentiment; Forward-Looking vs backward; Category (M&A, charitable donation, etc.); Political Bias; Journalistic Beat.
66	
67	**Downloads:** original 2024 export superseded by the `NOSIBLE/financial-sentiment` HF dataset (100,000 cleaned, deduplicated, labeled samples).
68	
69	### 4. BUILD RECIPE (educational scale)
70	
71	1. Assemble a corpus of financial news headlines+descriptions (a few thousand rows from an open dataset or synthetic sample). [inferred — replica lacks the NOSIBLE index; assume any diverse financial news source]
72	2. Stratify sampling across year × category × industry cells, taking top-N per cell by a "coverage" proxy; apply the quality filters (title 5–25 words, description 10–50 words, dedup). [disclosed — SQL given; the coverage metric must be approximated, e.g., by story duplication count]
73	3. Hand-label ~250 random stories as {−1, 0, +1}. [disclosed]
74	4. Implement classifiers: TextBlob and VADER with 3 thresholds each; Flair with 70/80/90% confidence gating for the neutral class; `ProsusAI/finbert`, `yiyanghkust/finbert-tone`, `Sigma/financial-sentiment-analysis` via `transformers`. [disclosed]
75	5. Implement LLM labeling with the exact few-shot prompt from the post (POS/NEU/NEG, default-to-NEU rule, 9 examples), using any modern API models as stand-ins for PaLM-2/GPT-4. [disclosed prompt; inferred model substitution]
76	6. Compute the pairwise agreement matrix (percent exact 3-class label match) across all models plus humans; order rows by human agreement. [disclosed]
77	7. Record per-story cost and latency per API model; extrapolate to a large-corpus cost figure. [disclosed protocol; use current pricing]
78	8. Add a random-label baseline for post-test probability computation. [disclosed]
79	
80	### 5. GAPS
81	
82	- The 250 human labels and the labeling rubric/guidelines the humans used are not published.
83	- Exact agreement-matrix numbers exist only as images; only a handful of cells are quoted in prose.
84	- API hyperparameters (temperature, max tokens) for the LLM calls are unstated ("defaults" for PaLM only).
85	- How ties/refusals/malformed LLM outputs were handled is not described.
86	- The precise definition/computation of `media_coverage`, `source_language_rank`, `source_variance_rank`, `apex_story`, and the 30-category/145-industry taxonomies are proprietary.
87	- Latency measurement methodology (the 339× VADER-vs-FinBERT claim) is not detailed.
88	
89	---
