328	| Section 232 steel & aluminium | 2018-03 | 18 / 34 / 11 |
329	| China Section 301 round one | 2018-06 | 22 / 28 / 4 |
330	| Aug 2019 escalation | 2019-08 | 19 / 15 / 10 |
331	| Phase One deal signed | 2020-01 | 38 / 30 / 53 |
332	| IEEPA tariffs Canada/Mexico/China | 2025-02 | 7 / 11 / 5 |
333	| Liberation Day | 2025-04 | 1 / 1 / 1 |
334	| Geneva truce | 2025-05 | 2 / 3 / 6 |
335	| IEEPA Supreme Court hearing | 2025-11 | 14 / 7 / 44 |
336	| IEEPA struck down | 2026-02 | 11 / 9 / 15 |
337	
338	**Polarity axis**
339	- Events clearly not about trade average weight **0.44** (just below neutral 0.5); events passing the trade filter average **0.63**. Among counted events: **60% above 0.6** (clearly uncertain), **21% below 0.4** (clearly settled), the remaining fifth neutral.
340	- `net_polarity(t) = Σ breadth(e)·polarity(e) / Σ breadth(e)` over relevant events on day t (verbatim).
341	- Smoother: fast **3-day half-life** when polarity jumps ≥ **1.5 standard deviations** above its trailing year (no look-ahead); slow **30-day half-life** on calm days and moves toward resolution. The asymmetry captures spikes quickly.
342	- Readings: **+0.59** at the 2018 China 301 escalation; **+0.48** on Liberation Day; near zero through the quiet stretch of 2021; negative when the Phase One deal is signed (Jan 2020). The sign distinguishes a resolved dispute from a quiet news week — something a level-only keyword index cannot do.
343	
344	**Tariff-rate lead check**
345	- Realized US tariff rate = customs duties ÷ imports of goods, quarterly BEA NIPA tables via DBnomics. 2018–19: 1.4% → 3%; 2025: 2.6% → **12.8%** (largest move since the 1970s/Nixon era).
346	- Each index's level vs next-quarter change in tariff rate: **TPU 0.61, BBD 0.59, NOSIBLE 0.66**. Higher uncertainty tends to be followed by higher tariffs.
347	
348	**Misses**
349	- 2018–19 magnitude ~2× the published index after rebasing (that trade war was a larger share of a global, then-smaller corpus than of seven US/UK papers; timing matches).
350	- Late-2025 litigation under-scored: litigation drew far less trade-relevant coverage than the active tariff actions. Nov 2025 oral arguments: TPU rank 14 vs NOSIBLE 44; Feb 2026 ruling realigns: NOSIBLE 15 vs TPU 11.
351	
352	**EPU extension — two disclosed design lessons**
353	1. A single generic "economic policy uncertainty" sentence **fails**: the defining US events of April 2020 (Fed cutting rates to zero, first shutdown orders) embed as concrete acts, not the abstract idea, scoring below any usable cutoff → the fix is a list of concrete decision types (10 levers, each written as a few concrete sentences).
354	2. A single generic uncertain/certain pair is lopsided across topics: uncertainty shares a vocabulary across topics ("may", "unclear", "stalled") but resolution is always written as the topic's own concrete act ("signs the bill", "imposes the tariffs", "cuts rates"); articles rarely say "policy is now certain" → every lever gets a **matched U/C pair**, one framing the decision as proposed/threatened/undecided, the other as done and in force.
355	
356	**EPU formulas (verbatim)**
357	```
358	relevant(e) = max cosine(event e, all lever sentences) >= 0.35
359	polarity(e) = tanh((uncertain_sim - certain_sim) / 0.1)   # within the best-matching pair
360	w_unc(e)    = (1 + polarity(e)) / 2
361	
362	NOSIBLE-EPU(t) = Σ breadth(e)·w_unc(e) over relevant US events in month t
363	                 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
364	                 trailing 12-month average of total US-attributed monthly breadth
365	```
366	- Appendix scoring rules: a lever's score = the highest of its two framings; relevance = highest score over all levers; each event's polarity comes from the pair whose better framing scores highest. Category threshold **0.25**.
367	- US attribution = the event's tagged primary country is the United States; both numerator and denominator US-scoped ("we scale US attention by US attention, the way the published index scales US articles by US articles").
368	- The 10th lever (shutting down/reopening the economy) exists because embeddings don't get COVID "for free" the way keyword counts do (every closure article incidentally had an economy word, a policy word, and an uncertainty word; an event embeds as its core meaning). Written in timeless terms, nothing pandemic-specific, and kept as a separate diagnostic line — the entire COVID gap (large positive Mar–May 2020, fading to nothing by mid-2021, no divergence anywhere else in eleven years) traces to that single lever.
369	
370	**EPU results (monthly level / change)**
371	
372	| target | level / change |
373	|---|---|
374	| The bar (paper's own two US variants) | 0.92 / 0.65 |
375	| US vs published US EPU | **0.77 / 0.53** |
376	| National security vs published categorical | 0.83 / 0.59 |
377	| Healthcare vs published categorical | 0.73 / 0.44 |
378	
379	- Both NOSIBLE-EPU and published rank April 2025 as the highest month of the eleven years; both put COVID spring 2020 and the 2025 tariff run in their top few. National security: April 2025 first in both (heavy sanctions-and-retaliation coverage), March 2025 and March 2026 close behind in both. Healthcare (the loosest of the four) agrees on COVID spring 2020 and the 2025 health-policy upheaval (Medicaid changes in the tax bill, ACA-subsidy fight, HHS leadership turnover), and catches the May 2017 ACA-repeal fight the keyword count ranks far down.
380	- The residual gap has one cause: counting words vs measuring events. Published EPU counts condition-driven coverage whenever it mentions policy (a record-unemployment article counts with incidental keywords); NOSIBLE counts only events that embed as policy decisions. So condition-driven months (spring 2020 jobless-claims records, late-2025 background tariff mentions) sit below the published series; NOSIBLE runs hotter on clear-cut decisions (February 2025 tariffs).
381	- Scaling advantage stated: one sentence set and one cutoff build the headline index and both categories at once (the paper hand-builds a word list per category); the same index runs for any country as a group-by on the country field, in every language ("adding a category or a country is nearly free").
382	- Measurement protocol (appendix): common window **2015-03 to 2026-05 monthly**, jointly non-null rows after rebasing each series to its own mean; published US EPU = the news-based Fig-1 series from policyuncertainty.com; categorical series = the "National security" and "Health care" columns of their categorical file.
383	
384	**Full 60-sentence EPU anchor set**: disclosed verbatim in the post's appendix — levers and pair counts: MONETARY ×3 pairs, TAXES ×2, SPENDING ×2, DEBT ×2, ENTITLEMENTS ×1, REGULATION ×2, FINANCIAL REGULATION ×2, TRADE ×3, MAJOR ECONOMIC POLICY ACTIONS ×3, SHUTTING DOWN THE ECONOMY ×2, CATEGORY: NATIONAL SECURITY ×4, CATEGORY: HEALTHCARE ×4. Copy directly from the archive file, lines 176–317. Example pair (trade lever), verbatim:
385	```
386	tariffs, uncertain:  "The government is threatening or proposing to impose, raise,
387	                      suspend or lift tariffs, but it is unclear what it will actually do."
388	tariffs, certain:    "The government has imposed, raised, suspended or lifted tariffs,
389	                      and the tariff decision has taken effect."
390	```
391	
392	**Future-work admissions**: anchor sets are hand-written, calibrated against a single benchmark, "deliberate but unoptimized" (whether anchors are best hand-authored, corpus-mined, or learned against the benchmark is open); the signed axis maps the similarity gap through a fixed monotone transform (`tanh(gap/0.1)`), a modeling choice not a result — a calibrated or learned mapping is the stated next step. Both directions evaluable against the published benchmarks.
393	
394	### 4. BUILD RECIPE
395	
396	1. **Corpus** [inferred]: deduped news events with dates, breadth proxy, and (for EPU) a primary-country tag — use NER-majority country or source-domain country as proxy [inferred assumption].
397	2. **Embed events** [disclosed model]: `text-embedding-3-large` → keep first 1,024 dims, L2-normalise. [inferred substitute]: multilingual sentence-transformers (e.g., `bge-m3` or `paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2`); re-sweep the 0.35 threshold against the published index if substituting (the post itself says 0.35 came from such a sweep).
398	3. **Embed the 5 TPU anchors verbatim** [disclosed]: same model, truncation, normalisation as the events.
399	4. **Score** [disclosed scale]: batched numpy cosine (`events @ anchors.T` on normalised vectors); the 12-minutes-on-a-laptop figure confirms brute force suffices at ~15M × 1024-d.
400	5. **Gate & weight** [disclosed]: `relevant = topic_max >= 0.35`; `polarity = tanh((u − c)/0.1)`; `w = (1+polarity)/2`.
401	6. **Daily TPU** [disclosed]: pandas groupby-day Σ `breadth·w` over relevant events ÷ trailing 12-month rolling mean of total daily breadth [inferred: exact rolling-window mechanics unstated].
402	7. **Monthly series & correlations** [disclosed protocol]: aggregate to monthly [inferred: mean of daily values], rebase each series to its own mean, correlate levels and first differences on jointly non-null months, window 2015-03–2026-05; also compute quarterly.
403	8. **Benchmarks** [disclosed sources]: TPU from matteoiacoviello.com/tpu.htm; EPU headline + categorical files from policyuncertainty.com; tariff rate from BEA NIPA via DBnomics.
404	9. **Polarity chart** [disclosed]: daily breadth-weighted mean polarity; implement the asymmetric EWM smoother — half-life 3 days when the day's polarity ≥ trailing-year mean + 1.5·std [inferred: "trailing year" = 252 trading or 365 calendar days, unstated], else half-life 30 days.
405	10. **EPU** [disclosed]: embed the 60 appendix sentences; lever score = max(U, C); relevance = max over levers ≥ 0.35; polarity from best-matching pair; US-only numerator and denominator; categories add the 0.25 category-pair gate.
406	11. **Validate** [disclosed]: episode ranks (April 2025 = #1 everywhere; 12 episodes above the 60th percentile), threshold sensitivity sweep 0.30→0.40 (~0.02 correlation change), tariff-rate next-quarter-change lead correlation.
407	
408	### 5. GAPS
409	
410	- Coverage-peak dating algorithm (how "the day its coverage peaked" is computed).
411	- What event text is embedded and the multilingual embedding pipeline.
412	- Dedup/breadth machinery (proprietary, as in all posts).
413	- Exact daily→monthly aggregation and the precise definition of "trailing 12-month average" (calendar vs trading days, min-periods, warm-up handling).
414	- The sweep that produced 0.35 (grid, metric); why 0.25 for categories; why temperature 0.1 in the tanh (acknowledged as an uncalibrated modeling choice).
415	- How the primary country is tagged upstream.
416	- Whether the 0.86 daily correlation is on raw dailies or the 30-day moving averages (chart caption is ambiguous).
417	- No code, no raw index values.
418	
419	---
420	
421	## Cross-Post Synthesis (for the build guide)
422	
423	All three posts are instances of **one template** with five knobs:
424	
425	1. **Concept definition**: an ontology-code filter (GPR), or K anchor phrases embedded once (stress: 17, TPU: 5, EPU: 60, oil: 3, trade coercion: 1). Anchors must be entity- and time-agnostic to avoid hindsight.
426	2. **Admission rule**: hard topic filter; `max-cosine ≥ floor` (floors used: 0.30 stress, 0.30 oil, 0.35 TPU/EPU, 0.40 trade-coercion, 0.25 EPU categories); or hybrid (`ontology OR embedding` for trade, `ontology AND embedding` for oil).
427	3. **Weight**: `breadth`, `relevance × breadth`, or `breadth × w_unc` (signed-polarity tilt via `tanh((u−c)/0.1)`).
428	4. **Denominator**: same-day total breadth (share) or trailing 12-month average of total breadth (detrended share) — always attention-normalized so corpus growth cancels; global denominator for country cuts, country-scoped denominator for EPU's US/US normalization.
429	5. **Post-processing**: rebase-to-mean for benchmark comparison; or the full causal trading stack (7d trailing mean → 252d robust z via 1.4826·MAD → EWMA span 7 → 2-day lag → hysteresis state machine with embargoed, plateau-selected thresholds).
430	
431	The consistent proprietary moat — the deliberate gap in every post — is the upstream event layer: de-duplication into single event records, `total_netlocs` breadth, topic/country tagging, and event dating. An educational replica's main engineering work is approximating that layer (cluster headlines by embedding similarity; breadth = distinct source domains); everything downstream is fully disclosed formulas implementable in a few hundred lines of pandas + numpy + one embedding model.
432

# Clean-Room Reverse-Engineering Notes: Three NOSIBLE Blog Posts

Sources (archived, all content © NOSIBLE, educational study only):

- `/Users/neelanpather/dev/cybernaut_mini/docs/blog-archive/rebuilding-the-geopolitical-risk-index-from-nosible-world.md` (Matthew Dicks, 2026-06-06)
- `/Users/neelanpather/dev/cybernaut_mini/docs/blog-archive/turning-news-into-a-risk-on-risk-off-equity-signal.md` (Gareth Warburton, 2026-06-16)
- `/Users/neelanpather/dev/cybernaut_mini/docs/blog-archive/an-embedding-based-approach-to-trade-and-economic-policy-uncertainty.md` (Matthew Dicks, 2026-06-17)

Shared substrate across all three posts: the NOSIBLE World event database — de-duplicated news events (one real-world event = one record), each carrying (a) an OpenAI `text-embedding-3-large` embedding in field `oai_vector` (3,072-d, Matryoshka-trained so the first 1,024 dims are a valid embedding), (b) publisher breadth in field `total_netlocs` (number of distinct publishers that covered the event), (c) a date, (d) a single IPTC Media Topics topic (`iptc_level_1/2/3`), (e) a main country, and (f) NER-extracted geopolitical entities in `ent_gpe`. The universal design pattern: **share of breadth-weighted publisher attention matching a concept, normalized by a corpus-growth-robust denominator**.

---

## Post 1 — "We Rebuilt the Geopolitical Risk Index with Nosible World"

### 1. WHAT IT IS

A replication of the Federal Reserve Geopolitical Risk (GPR) index — both the original Caldara & Iacoviello (2018/2022) keyword-count version and the newer AI-GPR (Iacoviello & Tong, 2026) LLM-scored version — built purely from metadata already attached to NOSIBLE's de-duplicated multilingual event database: IPTC topic tags, NER country entities, publisher breadth, and (for two gap-filling extensions) stored embeddings. It solves the problem that "geopolitical risk is a feeling, not a figure": producing a live daily/monthly numeric risk series (global, per-country, per-country-pair, and oil-supply) that quant/risk models can consume, with no LLM reading each article and no keyword lists — matching the published benchmarks at correlations of ~0.90–0.99.

### 2. ARCHITECTURE

1. **Event store (input)** — NOSIBLE World database, 2010–present; study window 2019+ (overlap with published indices), 13.2M de-duplicated events. Each event: IPTC 3-level topic, main country, `ent_gpe` NER entities, `total_netlocs` breadth, `oai_vector` embedding, date.
2. **Geopolitical classifier (rule filter)** — exact match on IPTC ontology *codes* (never label words):
   - `iptc_level_1 == "conflict, war and peace"` OR
   - `iptc_level_2 == "international relations"` OR
   - `iptc_level_3 in {"war crime", "genocide", "terrorism", "nuclear policy"}`
3. **Global index aggregation** — per day, breadth-weighted share: sum of `total_netlocs` over geopolitical events ÷ sum over all events. One group-by over the event table.
4. **Detrending variant** — same numerator; denominator swapped to a trailing 12-month average of total attention (removes corpus-growth drift). This detrended version is carried through the rest of the post.
5. **Rescaling (display only)** — each series rescaled to average 100 over 2020–2024; correlations unchanged.
6. **Country attribution layer** — resolve `ent_gpe` entity strings to countries (whole-string, case-insensitive match against a table of country names, official aliases, nationalities ≥4 letters, native-language names; partial matches rejected; ambiguous strings like bare "Georgia" dropped). Attribution set = main country + all resolved NER countries. Explode events to attribution sets → group by (country, month) → divide by global denominator `B(m)` = trailing 12-month average of total monthly breadth.
7. **Bilateral (pair) layer** — self-join each event's attribution set into unordered pairs → group by (pair, month) → same `B(m)`.
8. **Embedding rescue path #1 (trade coercion)** — one anchor phrase embedded; event admitted if `geopolitical(e) OR cosine(event, anchor) >= 0.40`. Fixes the China–USA gap (tariff events are IPTC "international trade", economy branch).
9. **Embedding rescue path #2 (Oil-GPR)** — three oil-supply anchor phrases; `relevance(e)` = max cosine; keep events that are geopolitical AND `relevance(e) >= 0.30`; weight by `relevance(e) × breadth(e)`; divide by `B(m)`. Per-region versions attribute surviving events to producer regions/countries as in step 6.
10. **Validation** — Pearson correlation vs published GPR / AI-GPR series, on levels and month-over-month changes; z-scored per-region charts for oil.

### 3. CONCRETE TECHNICAL FACTS

**Benchmarks & context**
- Original GPR (Caldara & Iacoviello 2018; AER 112(4), 2022): counts geopolitical-risk words across **ten major newspapers**, as a share of all articles; reaches back over a century. Data at matteoiacoviello.com/gpr.htm.
- AI-GPR (Iacoviello & Tong 2026): an LLM scores each article's geopolitical risk **from zero to one**; adds per-country, per-pair, and oil-supply cuts. This is the target NOSIBLE holds itself to.
- Institutional users named: Federal Reserve (maintains it), IMF GFSR April 2025 Ch.2 and WEO April 2026 Ch.1, ECB/ESRB January 2026 fragmentation report.
- The two published versions agree with each other "at about the same level" as NOSIBLE reaches.

**Data**
- Database covers 2010–today; study uses 2019 onward; **13.2 million de-duplicated events**.
- One real event = one record regardless of outlet count; `total_netlocs` = distinct publisher count = `breadth(e)`.
- Multilingual; no per-article LLM pass; no keyword list.

**Geopolitical filter (verbatim)**
```
geopolitical(e) is TRUE when ANY of these hold:
    iptc_level_1 == "conflict, war and peace"
    iptc_level_2 == "international relations"
    iptc_level_3 in { "war crime", "genocide", "terrorism", "nuclear policy" }
```
- Matched on ontology codes exactly, never label words ("weather warning", "tug-of-war" cannot leak in).
- IPTC Media Topics: structured three-level hierarchy; top-level buckets include `conflict, war and peace`, `economy, business and finance`, `health`.

**Global index formula (verbatim)**
```
NOSIBLE-GPR(t) = sum of breadth(e) over geopolitical events on day t
                 ------------------------------------------------------
                 sum of breadth(e) over all events on day t
```
- A story carried by 200 outlets counts as one event weighted by 200, never as 200 separate events.
- Charts rescaled so each series averages 100 over 2020–2024 (leaves correlations unchanged).
- Two denominators: same-day total attention (raw) vs trailing 12-month average of total attention (detrended). Detrend motivation: the corpus grew and broadened 2019→2026, so raw shares drift down even when the world is no calmer; the benchmark's small stable newspaper set has no such drift.

**Global correlations vs AI-GPR**: raw daily share **0.90 levels / 0.79 month-to-month changes**; detrended **0.89 / 0.75**.
- Events verified visually: Soleimani 2020, Ukraine invasion 2022, Israel–Gaza 2023, Iran–Israel 2024, US–Iran war 2026.

**Country index**
- Formula: `GPR(country c, month m) = Σ breadth(e) over geopolitical events in month m where c ∈ attribution(e) / B(m)`, with `attribution(e) = {main country} ∪ {countries resolved from named entities}`.
- `B(m)` = **global** trailing 12-month average of total monthly breadth across all events (not a country's own coverage — a country's own coverage spikes in a crisis and would cancel the signal; the trailing average also stops corpus growth masking real spikes).
- Entity→country resolution handles: names/abbreviations (United States, U.S., USA), nationalities (American, Russian, Israeli), other languages/scripts (中国, Россия, ישראל). Whole-string, case-insensitive matching; nationalities must be ≥4 letters; partial matches never count (`Indiana` never → India); genuinely ambiguous strings such as bare `Georgia` are dropped.
- The US is named in roughly **one third** of all geopolitical news; multi-country attribution lifts the US correlation **0.45 → 0.83**.
- Correlations: **Iran 0.99, Israel 0.96, Ukraine 0.96, Russia 0.94; 76 countries above 0.60**. (AI-GPR needs an extra LLM pass over every article to get this; NOSIBLE gets it from existing tags.)

**Pair index**
- `GPR(pair a-b, m) = Σ breadth(e) over geopolitical events in month m naming BOTH a and b / B(m)`; unordered pairs via self-join of each event's attribution set. Same `B(m)`.
- Correlations: **Iran–USA 0.97, Russia–Ukraine 0.95, India–Pakistan 0.95**. Failure: **China–USA 0.28** (a tariff story gets topic "international trade", in the economy branch of the ontology, invisible to the conflict filter; simply adding the trade topic would drown the signal in routine commerce).

**Trade-coercion fix**
- Anchor phrase (verbatim): *"Tariffs, trade wars and economic coercion between countries: a government imposing import tariffs, retaliatory duties, export controls or other trade restrictions on another country, and the diplomatic tensions and threats of retaliation these trigger"*
- Admission rule: `geopolitical(e) OR trade(e) >= 0.40` (cosine between event embedding and anchor). Everything else identical (same breadth weight, country attribution, denominator).
- Results: China country score **0.53 → 0.78**; China–USA pair **0.28 → 0.75**. Only **8,079 events added** across the entire corpus (one real trade-war event, weighted by breadth, carries a spike). Conflict countries (Ukraine, Russia, Israel, Iran) unmoved. April 2025 tariff spike, missing before, now appears.

**Oil-GPR**
- AI-GPR paper's method: keep geopolitical articles → filter to oil mentions → LLM asks whether each describes an oil supply disruption, and in which region. NOSIBLE replaces the keyword filter and disruption model with embeddings in one step, no extra model call.
- Direction subtlety stated: broad geopolitical risk usually *lowers* the oil price (fear cuts demand); risk inside oil-producing regions *raises* it (threatens supply). A useful signal must isolate the supply side.
- Three anchor phrases (verbatim):
  1. "Armed conflict and war in or around major oil-producing regions"
  2. "Crude oil supply: OPEC production quotas, output levels and disruptions to oil production or exports"
  3. "Sanctions, embargoes and export restrictions on major oil-exporting countries such as Iran, Russia and Venezuela"
- Formula: `Oil-GPR(m) = Σ relevance(e) × breadth(e) over events in month m that are geopolitical AND relevance(e) >= 0.30 / B(m)`, where `relevance(e)` = highest cosine vs the three anchors.
- Correlations vs published academic Oil-GPR: **same-day 0.95; 12-month detrended 0.97**.
- Per-region (monthly, z-scored): **Middle East 0.95, Venezuela 0.96, United States 0.92, Russia 0.91; Africa 0.44, North Sea 0.04** (published series itself near noise in the weak regions over this window). Russia's signal jumps in 2022 with the invasion of Ukraine.
- Explicit scope limit: they match the academic risk index, not the oil price itself; demonstrating the price/output shock from the NOSIBLE signal is left to future work.

**Generalization claims**: the same template extends to economic policy uncertainty, stock-market volatility (vs the VIX), climate concern and pandemic risk (ontology engine); and gold, natural gas, wheat, copper, freight/shipping, individual currencies (embedding engine — "the same few lines of code").

### 4. BUILD RECIPE (educational scale)

1. **Corpus** [inferred — post uses proprietary NOSIBLE data]: use GDELT or an open news archive spanning several years. Assumption: any dated multi-source corpus works; de-duplicate by clustering near-identical headlines (embedding cosine > ~0.9 within a date window) and set `breadth(e)` = number of distinct source domains in the cluster (proxy for `total_netlocs`).
2. **Topic tagging** [inferred substitute]: NOSIBLE uses pre-tagged IPTC codes. Replicate with zero-shot classification into IPTC buckets via sentence-transformers (embed IPTC label descriptions, assign nearest), or skip the ontology and use an embedding anchor for the geopolitical concept itself (consistent with the post's own "second engine").
3. **Geopolitical filter** [disclosed]: implement the exact three-clause rule on your topic labels.
4. **Global daily index** [disclosed]: pandas group-by day; numerator = Σ breadth over geopolitical events; denominator = Σ breadth over all events.
5. **Detrended variant** [disclosed]: denominator = trailing 12-month rolling mean of total breadth.
6. **Rescale for charts** [disclosed]: rebase each series to mean 100 over a common window (post uses 2020–2024).
7. **NER + country resolution** [disclosed method, inferred tooling]: spaCy NER (GPE entities) if the corpus lacks tags; build a country alias table (pycountry + manual aliases + nationalities ≥4 chars + native names); whole-string case-insensitive matching; drop ambiguous strings.
8. **Country & pair indices** [disclosed]: explode to attribution sets, group by (country, month) and (unordered pair, month), divide by global `B(m)`.
9. **Embedding anchors** [disclosed method]: embed the verbatim trade-coercion and oil phrases. [inferred] With sentence-transformers instead of `text-embedding-3-large`, the 0.40/0.30 thresholds will NOT transfer — recalibrate from the score histogram or sweep against the published index.
10. **Trade-OR and Oil-AND rules** [disclosed]: `geopolitical OR trade≥θ` for the trade fix; `geopolitical AND relevance≥θ`, weight `relevance × breadth`, for oil.
11. **Validation** [disclosed]: download published GPR/AI-GPR series from matteoiacoviello.com; Pearson correlation on monthly levels and first differences on jointly non-null dates; z-score per-region series for plots.

### 5. GAPS (not revealed)

- The event de-duplication algorithm (most load-bearing upstream step).
- How IPTC topics and the single "main country" are assigned (model, prompt, accuracy).
- The full country-alias table and complete ambiguous-string drop list.
- How an event's date is set.
- What text is embedded per event and the multilingual embedding pipeline.
- How thresholds 0.40 (trade) and 0.30 (oil) were selected (no sweep described in this post).
- The producer-region → country mapping for Oil-GPR regions.
- Exact daily→monthly aggregation for the monthly indices (sum vs mean of daily shares).
- No code, no raw index values.

---

## Post 2 — "Turning News into a Risk-On/Risk-Off Equity Signal"

### 1. WHAT IT IS

A daily market-stress gauge built by scoring every de-duplicated news event's stored embedding against 17 fixed "market stress" anchor phrases, converting the breadth-weighted share of stressful attention into a strictly-trailing robust z-score, and driving a two-state (equities vs T-bills) overlay strategy from it. Problem solved: turning qualitative news flow into a causal, tradeable risk-off trigger. On the S&P 500 over an untouched 2015–2026 test window the overlay keeps ~buy-and-hold's total return (+254% vs +269%) while cutting max drawdown from −34% to −18% and raising Sharpe from 0.64 to 0.89; the identical frozen rule transfers to the Nasdaq and Russell 2000. The post explicitly claims full reproducibility from the disclosed parameters plus the event database and EODHD prices. "The point is risk, not return."

### 2. ARCHITECTURE

1. **Inputs** — per de-duplicated event: `oai_vector` (`text-embedding-3-large`), `total_netlocs`, date; full daily history.
2. **Anchor bank** — 17 short stress concepts, each embedded once with the same model; entity- and time-agnostic (no specific countries, crises, or dates) so no hindsight enters the backtest.
3. **Dimensionality** — truncate both event vectors and anchors to the **first 1024 of 3,072 Matryoshka dims**, then **L2-renormalise**.
4. **Per-event scoring** — `relevance(e)` = max cosine over the 17 anchors; event counts only if `relevance(e) >= 0.30`.
5. **Daily intensity** — Σ `relevance(e)·breadth(e)` over qualifying events ÷ Σ `breadth(e)` over ALL events that day.
6. **Causal calibration** — (a) 7-day trailing mean; (b) robust z with trailing 252-trading-day median and MAD × 1.4826; (c) EWMA span 7. None uses future data.
7. **Lag & execution** — signal lagged 2 trading days before it can trigger; positions execute on the next bar.
8. **Two-state rule** — LONG equities; exit to `BIL.US` when z > 1.75; re-enter when out ≥ 5 days AND z < 0.25; cost 1 bp × |Δweight| per position change.
9. **Selection harness** — grid sweep on 2010–2013 train window only, objective = Sortino improvement over buy-and-hold, one-year (252-day) embargo, plateau selection (median of top-20% cells), then frozen.
10. **Validation** — sanity overlay vs VIX (not part of strategy); backtests on GSPC, IXIC, IWM with EODHD adjusted closes, daily log returns.

### 3. CONCRETE TECHNICAL FACTS

**The 17 anchors (verbatim, name → phrase)**
```
credit_spreads     Widening corporate credit spreads, surging default risk and stress in corporate bond markets
liquidity          A liquidity crisis or funding stress freezing financial markets
deleveraging       Forced selling, margin calls, deleveraging and liquidations cascading through markets
recession          Rising fears of recession, sharp economic slowdown or collapsing growth
banking_credit     A banking crisis, credit crunch, defaults or financial-system instability
volatility_fear    A surge in financial market volatility, fear, panic and investor anxiety
equity_selloff     A sharp sell-off, crash or plunge in global stock markets
flight_to_safety   A flight to safety and risk-off panic: investors dumping risky assets for government bonds, gold and reserve currencies
sovereign_fx       A sovereign-debt default or currency crisis destabilising markets
monetary_shock     An unexpected hawkish central bank or interest-rate shock tightening financial conditions
rates_turmoil      Turmoil in government bond markets: a bond rout, spiking yields and surging interest-rate volatility
tail_hedging       Investors rushing to buy downside protection and hedge against a market crash; spiking demand for portfolio insurance
earnings_distress  A wave of corporate profit warnings, earnings misses, bankruptcies and corporate distress
employment_shock   A labour-market shock: surging unemployment, mass layoffs or a sharply weakening jobs report
tariffs            New import tariffs, escalating protectionism and a trade war between major economies
natural_disaster   A major natural disaster, extreme-weather catastrophe or critical-infrastructure failure disrupting the economy
war_conflict       The outbreak or escalation of war, military conflict or a major geopolitical security crisis
```

**Signal math (verbatim)**
```
intensity(t) = Σ over events on day t with relevance(e) ≥ 0.30 of relevance(e)·breadth(e)
               ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
               Σ over all events on day t of breadth(e)
```
- Embedding: 3,072-d `text-embedding-3-large`; first 1024 dims kept (Matryoshka training makes the prefix a complete embedding), L2-renormalised.
- Share not count → immune to crawl-volume drift; breadth as weight → a 200-outlet story counts once, weighted by 200.
- Relevance scores pile up near zero (most news is not about market stress). Example qualifying headlines: 0.57 → `tariffs` ("Trump Tariff Threats on Greenland Spark Global Trade War Fears"); 0.45 → `employment_shock` ("US Jobless Claims Rise Marginally While Q3 Productivity Surges").

**Calibration (verbatim)**
```
1. s(t) = 7-day trailing mean of intensity(t)              (settle daily noise)
2. z(t) = (s(t) - median) / (1.4826 * MAD)                 (median and MAD over the trailing
                                                            252 trading days; 1.4826 puts it
                                                            in sigma units)
3. z(t) = EWMA(z, span = 7)                                (so the position does not flicker)
```

**Trading rule (verbatim)**
```
state = LONG (fully in equities)
  if state == LONG and z > 1.75:          -> OUT (move to BIL.US), days_out = 0
  if state == OUT:
      days_out += 1
      if days_out >= 5 and z < 0.25:      -> LONG
cost = 1 bp charged on |w(t) - w(t-1)| each time the position changes
```
- News lagged **2 trading days**; execution next bar. Defensive leg `BIL.US` (SPDR 1-3 Month T-Bill ETF); overlay earns equity return when long, T-bill return when out.

**Parameter selection**
- Train: 2010–2013. Embargo: one year (252 trading days) so no test-period calibration window overlaps training data. Test: **2015-01-02 to 2026-06-01**, untouched by selection.
- Grid: `exit_z ∈ {1.75, 2.0, 2.25, 2.5, 2.75, 3.0}`; `enter_z ∈ {0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75}`; `min_hold ∈ {3, 5, 10, 15}` days.
- Objective: **Sortino improvement over buy-and-hold** (improvement, not raw level, so the choice rewards timing rather than equity exposure).
- Plateau not peak: take top 20% of cells by train score; set each parameter to the grid value nearest that set's median. Frozen result: exit 1.75 / enter 0.25 / hold 5.
- Full frozen parameter set (verbatim): relevance floor 0.30, rolling-mean window 7, robust-z window 252, EWMA span 7, news lag 2 trading days, exit z 1.75, enter z 0.25, min hold 5 days, 1 bp/turn, defensive leg BIL.US.

**Results (2015–2026 test)**

| Market | Sharpe B&H → overlay | Max DD B&H → overlay | Total return B&H → overlay |
|---|---|---|---|
| S&P 500 (GSPC) | +0.64 → +0.89 | −34% → −18% | +269% → +254% |
| Nasdaq Composite (IXIC) | +0.72 → +0.94 | −36% → −19% | +479% → +440% |
| Russell 2000 (IWM) | +0.41 → +0.67 | −41% → −22% | +186% → +254% |

- S&P Sortino: 0.77 → 1.01. Out of equities ~**a quarter of the time**, across **27 short episodes**, turnover **under five round-trips/year**.
- Improvement shows in both halves of the test period in all three markets (opposite of an overfit rule decaying out-of-sample).
- Episodes: stepped out ahead of the 2020 COVID crash and back in as it passed. 2025 tariff shock: z crossed the exit line in early February, overlay sat out the ~19% peak-to-trough drop to the April low, re-entered late May once z fell under the re-enter line; it gave up part of the rebound ("That is the cost").
- VIX sanity check: calibrated z co-moves with the VIX through the major episodes (2011, 2015, 2020, 2022) with no price data in the signal. VIX not part of the strategy.
- Honest accounting: reduces drawdown; will not beat a strong bull market; a sell-off that recovers costs return.

**Data sources**: NOSIBLE event DB (`oai_vector`, `total_netlocs`, date) over the full daily history; EODHD end-of-day adjusted close: `GSPC.INDX`, `IXIC.INDX`, `IWM.US`, `BIL.US`, `VIX.INDX`. Returns are daily log returns.

## Post 3 — "An Embedding-Based Approach to Trade and Economic Policy Uncertainty"

### 1. WHAT IT IS

A reconstruction of two canonical keyword-count policy-uncertainty indices — the Fed's Trade Policy Uncertainty (TPU) index (Caldara, Iacoviello, Molligo, Prestipino & Raffo, *Journal of Monetary Economics* 2020) and Baker-Bloom-Davis's Economic Policy Uncertainty (EPU) index (*QJE* 2016), plus two EPU category indices (national security, healthcare) — using only cosine similarity between stored event embeddings and small hand-written anchor-sentence sets: 5 sentences for TPU, 60 for the EPU family. The keyword papers' "topic word AND uncertainty word" rule becomes a topic-relevance gate plus a **signed** uncertainty weight from an uncertain-vs-certain sentence pair via `tanh` of the similarity gap — giving the replica a directional resolved↔uncertain axis the published indices lack. Scoring 14.9M events (2015–2026) takes ~12 minutes on a laptop; TPU matches the published benchmark at 0.87 monthly levels / 0.82 monthly changes (the two official indices agree at 0.96 / 0.70 with each other), and EPU matches the published US series at 0.77 on monthly levels.

### 2. ARCHITECTURE

1. **Inputs** — per event: `oai_vector` (`text-embedding-3-large`, 3,072-d; first 1,024 kept via Matryoshka, L2-normalized "so cosine similarities stay meaningful"), `total_netlocs` breadth, date (day its coverage peaked), primary-country tag (for the US-only EPU).
2. **TPU anchor set** — 3 topic sentences (tariffs, agreements, disputes) + 2 axis sentences (uncertain, certain).
3. **Relevance gate** — `relevant(e) = max cosine(event, 3 topic phrases) >= 0.35`.
4. **Polarity/weight** — `polarity(e) = tanh((uncertain_sim − certain_sim)/0.1)` ∈ [−1, +1]; `w_unc(e) = (1 + polarity)/2` ∈ [0, 1].
5. **Daily index** — Σ `breadth(e)·w_unc(e)` over relevant events ÷ trailing 12-month average of total daily breadth (worldwide events, every language, for TPU — not a US subset).
6. **Net-polarity diagnostic** — breadth-weighted mean polarity over relevant events per day, with a state-dependent asymmetric smoother (fast 3-day half-life when polarity jumps ≥1.5σ above its trailing year with no look-ahead; slow 30-day half-life on calm days and moves toward resolution).
7. **EPU extension** — 10 policy "levers" (monetary policy, taxes, spending, debt and shutdowns, entitlements, regulation, financial regulation, trade, major economic laws, shutting down/reopening the economy), each a set of matched uncertain/certain sentence pairs; 60 sentences total. Lever score = max of its two framings; relevance = max over all levers ≥ 0.35; polarity from the best-matching pair. US-only numerator (US-attributed policy-relevant events) and denominator (trailing 12-month average of total US-attributed monthly breadth).
8. **Category indices** — national security & healthcare: event must additionally score ≥ **0.25** against that category's own sentence pairs (matching the paper's category definition).
9. **Validation** — monthly/quarterly Pearson correlations (levels and changes) vs published TPU, BBD trade EPU, published US EPU and categorical series, on 2015-03–2026-05 monthly, jointly non-null rows, each series rebased to its own mean; episode-rank checks (out of 135 months); lead-lag check vs the realized US tariff rate (BEA NIPA customs duties ÷ goods imports, via DBnomics).

### 3. CONCRETE TECHNICAL FACTS

**Benchmarks**
- Published TPU: an article counts if it contains a trade-policy word AND an uncertainty word; **seven major newspapers**; back to **1960**. April 2025: highest value in its 65-year history — **11.5% of all newspaper articles** about trade policy uncertainty.
- BBD trade-policy EPU: rival index, different newspapers/word lists. TPU~BBD agreement over the window: **0.96 levels / 0.70 changes** monthly (the "bar").
- BBD EPU (QJE 2016): article counts if it has an economy word AND a policy word AND an uncertainty word, across ten leading US newspapers. The paper's own two US variants (10-paper monthly vs ~1,500-paper Newsbank daily aggregated to monthly) agree at **0.92 / 0.65** (the EPU bar).

**Scale & performance**
- **14.9 million events**, 2015–2026, scored in **~12 minutes on a laptop**.
- TPU scored over every event worldwide, in every language; EPU restricted to US-primary-country events (the one exception).
- Published index dates articles by print day; NOSIBLE dates events by coverage-peak day.

**TPU anchors (verbatim)**
```
tariffs:     "Import tariffs and duties: a government imposing, raising, threatening
              or suspending tariffs, customs duties, import quotas, surcharges or fees
              on goods imported from other countries"
agreements:  "Trade negotiations, trade agreements and trade treaties between countries:
              free trade deals being negotiated, renegotiated, signed, ratified,
              suspended or abandoned, and trade talks between governments"
disputes:    "Trade disputes, trade wars and protectionism: retaliatory tariffs,
              anti-dumping measures, import barriers, export controls and restrictions,
              boycotts of foreign goods, and trade complaints before the WTO"
uncertain:   "Trade policy uncertainty: the outlook for tariffs, trade agreements and
              trade rules is uncertain, unclear and unpredictable; threatened tariffs
              may or may not happen, trade negotiations are stalled or at risk of
              collapse, and businesses cannot plan for what trade policy comes next"
certain:     "Trade policy certainty and stability: a trade agreement is concluded and
              ratified, a trade dispute is resolved, tariffs are removed or finalized,
              and governments give businesses a clear, settled and predictable trade
              policy outlook"
```

**TPU formulas (verbatim)**
```
relevant(e) = max cosine(event e, the 3 topic phrases) >= 0.35
polarity(e) = tanh((uncertain_sim - certain_sim) / 0.1)      # -1 resolved .. +1 uncertain
w_unc(e)    = (1 + polarity(e)) / 2                          # 0 .. 1

NOSIBLE-TPU(t) = Σ breadth(e)·w_unc(e) over relevant events on day t
                 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
                 trailing 12-month average of total daily breadth
```
- The denominator strips out corpus growth, same as the GPR post.
- The 0.35 cutoff is "not load-bearing": moving it 0.30→0.40 changes every correlation by **~0.02**. Appendix states 0.35 was **chosen by a sweep against the published US index** and applied unchanged to both categories.

**Misses**

**EPU extension — two disclosed design lessons**
1. A single generic "economic policy uncertainty" sentence **fails**: the defining US events of April 2020 (Fed cutting rates to zero, first shutdown orders) embed as concrete acts, not the abstract idea, scoring below any usable cutoff → the fix is a list of concrete decision types (10 levers, each written as a few concrete sentences).
2. A single generic uncertain/certain pair is lopsided across topics: uncertainty shares a vocabulary across topics ("may", "unclear", "stalled") but resolution is always written as the topic's own concrete act ("signs the bill", "imposes the tariffs", "cuts rates"); articles rarely say "policy is now certain" → every lever gets a **matched U/C pair**, one framing the decision as proposed/threatened/undecided, the other as done and in force.

**EPU formulas (verbatim)**
```
relevant(e) = max cosine(event e, all lever sentences) >= 0.35
polarity(e) = tanh((uncertain_sim - certain_sim) / 0.1)   # within the best-matching pair
w_unc(e)    = (1 + polarity(e)) / 2

NOSIBLE-EPU(t) = Σ breadth(e)·w_unc(e) over relevant US events in month t
                 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
                 trailing 12-month average of total US-attributed monthly breadth
```
- Appendix scoring rules: a lever's score = the highest of its two framings; relevance = highest score over all levers; each event's polarity comes from the pair whose better framing scores highest. Category threshold **0.25**.
- US attribution = the event's tagged primary country is the United States; both numerator and denominator US-scoped ("we scale US attention by US attention, the way the published index scales US articles by US articles").
- The 10th lever (shutting down/reopening the economy) exists because embeddings don't get COVID "for free" the way keyword counts do (every closure article incidentally had an economy word, a policy word, and an uncertainty word; an event embeds as its core meaning). Written in timeless terms, nothing pandemic-specific, and kept as a separate diagnostic line — the entire COVID gap (large positive Mar–May 2020, fading to nothing by mid-2021, no divergence anywhere else in eleven years) traces to that single lever.

## Cross-Post Synthesis (for the build guide)

All three posts are instances of **one template** with five knobs:

1. **Concept definition**: an ontology-code filter (GPR), or K anchor phrases embedded once (stress: 17, TPU: 5, EPU: 60, oil: 3, trade coercion: 1). Anchors must be entity- and time-agnostic to avoid hindsight.
2. **Admission rule**: hard topic filter; `max-cosine ≥ floor` (floors used: 0.30 stress, 0.30 oil, 0.35 TPU/EPU, 0.40 trade-coercion, 0.25 EPU categories); or hybrid (`ontology OR embedding` for trade, `ontology AND embedding` for oil).
3. **Weight**: `breadth`, `relevance × breadth`, or `breadth × w_unc` (signed-polarity tilt via `tanh((u−c)/0.1)`).
4. **Denominator**: same-day total breadth (share) or trailing 12-month average of total breadth (detrended share) — always attention-normalized so corpus growth cancels; global denominator for country cuts, country-scoped denominator for EPU's US/US normalization.
5. **Post-processing**: rebase-to-mean for benchmark comparison; or the full causal trading stack (7d trailing mean → 252d robust z via 1.4826·MAD → EWMA span 7 → 2-day lag → hysteresis state machine with embargoed, plateau-selected thresholds).

The consistent proprietary moat — the deliberate gap in every post — is the upstream event layer: de-duplication into single event records, `total_netlocs` breadth, topic/country tagging, and event dating. An educational replica's main engineering work is approximating that layer (cluster headlines by embedding similarity; breadth = distinct source domains); everything downstream is fully disclosed formulas implementable in a few hundred lines of pandas + numpy + one embedding model.

# Reverse-Engineering NOSIBLE: A Clean-Room Build Guide

**Purpose.** This is an educational field guide to every piece of technology NOSIBLE
has disclosed on its public blog. For each system it states *what was disclosed*, the
*exact formulas / hyperparameters* where given, an open-tool *build recipe* at
laptop scale, and the *deliberate gaps* you must approximate.

**Ground rules.**

- **Clean-room / educational only.** Everything here is derived from the 12 public
  posts archived in [`blog-archive/`](blog-archive/). No private data, credentials, or
  non-public interfaces were used. `cybernaut_mini` is unaffiliated with NOSIBLE and
  claims no benchmark parity.
- Every recipe step is tagged **[disclosed]** (stated in a post) or **[inferred]**
  (a gap the guide fills, with the assumption named). When a post prints an exact
  formula, prompt, or hyperparameter, it is quoted verbatim so the replica is faithful.
- The one component NOSIBLE never reveals — the upstream **event layer**
  (de-duplication into one-record-per-event, `total_netlocs` breadth, topic/country
  tagging, event dating) — is the moat behind almost every downstream number. Your main
  original engineering is approximating that layer; everything after it is disclosed math.

---

## 0. The NOSIBLE stack at a glance

Three product surfaces sit on one substrate.

```
                          ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
   Cybernaut-1 (agentic)  │  LLM-guided MCTS over "Hybrid-3"          │  §2
                          ├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
   Hybrid-3 search        │  8-stage multilingual retrieval pipeline │  §1
                          │  over a federation of 250,000 shards      │
                          ├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
   Enrichment / signals   │  NER + KG (§4), frozen-embedding features │  §5,§6,§7
                          │  (§5), distilled tiny classifiers (§3),   │
                          │  quant indices (§6)                       │
                          ├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
   Event layer (the moat) │  dedup → 1 record/event; breadth; IPTC    │  §8
                          │  topics; NER country; oai_vector; dating  │
                          └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Naming.** "Shards" (Road-to-Cybernaut post) and "collections" (faceted-search post)
are the same construct: ~250,000 semantically+lexically coherent, near-uniform mini
search engines learned from ~250M embeddings/documents. "Hybrid-3" is the 8-stage
pipeline; "Cybernaut-1" is the RL/MCTS agent on top of it.

**Recurring primitives worth memorizing** — they appear across unrelated posts:

- **RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion)** — the universal ensembling glue:
  `score(d) = Σ_i 1/(k + rank_i(d))`, `k=60` conventional (constant not disclosed).
- **Breadth-weighted attention share** — every quant signal is
  `Σ breadth·weight over matching events / (total breadth or its trailing 12-mo mean)`.
- **Frozen-embedding geometry** — cosine + tanh gate + power-mean / signed contrast,
  deliberately deterministic and backtest-safe (no LLM per document).
- **Ensemble → distil** — label with an LLM committee, then distill into a linear head
  or a 0.6B model that runs for ~$0.

---

## 1. Hybrid-3: the eight-stage retrieval pipeline

**Source:** `the-road-to-cybernaut-1.md`. **cybernaut_mini mapping:** this is the part
the repo already replicates — see `routing.py`, `retrieval.py`, `rrf.py`, `sharding.py`,
`indexing.py`, `expansion.py`, `providers/embeddings.py`.

### What was disclosed

A query flows through eight stages; each stage's tech stack is named in the post.

1. **Language detection & translation** — `fasttext-langdetect` (170+ langs);
   `gemma-3n-e4b-it` via OpenRouter for translation (140 langs).
2. **Multilingual tokenization** — a wrapper over ~12 NLP libs (spaCy, NLTK, BlingFire,
   pySBD, pyStemmer, jieba, mecab, wtpsplit, …): sentence-split, normalize, stem,
   stop-word removal. Claim: *well-calibrated lexical beats well-calibrated semantic on
   long high-intent AI queries; hybrid beats both.*
3. **Search-intent prediction** — extract "intents" = proximal token n-grams with a high
   **harmonic mean of per-token TF-IDF**, excluding function-word POS (pronouns,
   determiners, conjunctions, adverbs). Stack: NumPy, spaCy.
4. **Instruction tuning & embedding** — embed query + expansions with
   **`intfloat/multilingual-e5-large-instruct`** using an LLM-evolved instruction
   template. Disclosed template: *"Given a question, please retrieve any relevant
   {Language} Headlines, Leads, Passages, and Source URLs that focus on the same named
   entities as the question, and provide substantive answers to the question."* Claim:
   good instructions are worth **1–5%** precision/recall for free.
5. **Shard selection** — four ranking factors fused by RRF:
   (a) **vanilla dense** cosine(query, shard-summary embedding) over **HNSW**;
   (b) **Bayesian dense** — *proprietary, patent-pending, withheld*;
   (c) **vanilla sparse** TF-IDF keyword similarity;
   (d) **entity sparse** similarity. Stack: NumPy/SciPy/Numba/SimSIMD/USearch.
6. **Shard reranking** — RRF over: **bloom-filter** reranker (downrank shards whose
   phrase bloom filter never saw the query intents), **compression** reranker (the shard
   whose trained **Zstandard** dictionary compresses the query best wins), **neural**
   reranker (**`BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3`** over shard titles), **Personalized PageRank**
   over a shard kNN graph. LLM reranking works but "latency too high." Stack: Zstandard, rBloom.
7. **Shard-based query expansion** — each shard's co-occurrence **synonym graph**
   probabilistically expands terms; coherence disambiguates ("gene" only genetic here).
   Cap additions so originals aren't drowned. Stack: NumPy.
8. **Map-reduce retrieval** — broadcast to the top **10–30** shards; each runs
   SQL filter → BM25 lexical → semantic → fuse → full-text (Aho-Corasick) for intents;
   group by doc id; build user-length snippets; return ~100 results. Stack: Polars,
   SimSIMD, Numba, ahocorasick-rs.

### Concrete numbers

250,000 shards; ~1B webpages; last shard-training run = 250M embeddings; example shard
11,343: 134,523 docs / 8.4M words / vocab 64,992 / 2,523 keywords. Final routing = 10–30
shards, ~100 results.

### Build recipe (laptop scale)

1. **[disclosed]** Corpus → passages as JSONL `{id, text, metadata}`. **[inferred]**
   a few thousand–tens of thousands of docs.
2. **[disclosed]** Cluster into K coherent, near-uniform shards. **[inferred]** embed with
   `multilingual-e5-large-instruct` (or `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` for speed) and run
   **balanced/constrained KMeans** (`k-means-constrained`, or `MiniBatchKMeans` +
   post-balancing — which is what `sharding.py` does). *The proprietary segmentation model
   is unavailable; constrained clustering is the stand-in.*
3. **[disclosed]** Per shard build: BM25 (`rank_bm25`), a vector index (FAISS or
   `usearch`/HNSW), vocabulary, top-TF-IDF keywords, spaCy NER entities, a co-occurrence
   (PMI) synonym graph, a phrase **bloom filter** (`rbloom`), and a **Zstandard** dictionary
   (`zstandard.train_dictionary`).
4. **[disclosed]** Generate/collect an LLM summary per shard and embed it as the shard's
   dense descriptor. **[inferred]** fall back to the mean doc embedding if no LLM.
5. **[disclosed]** Stages 1–4 at query time: langdetect → tokenize (spaCy + snowball) →
   intents (harmonic-mean TF-IDF n-grams minus function words) → E5-instruct embed.
   **[inferred]** English-only build may skip translation.
6. **[disclosed]** Stage 5: fuse factors (a),(c),(d) with RRF; **omit (b)** (undisclosed).
   `score(d)=Σ 1/(60+rank_i(d))`. **[inferred]** `k=60` is the standard RRF constant.
7. **[disclosed]** Stage 6: bloom check + Zstd compression-ratio + `bge-reranker-v2-m3`
   cross-encoder over shard titles + optional Personalized PageRank (`networkx`); fuse with RRF.
8. **[disclosed]** Stage 7: expand via shard synonym graphs, capped.
9. **[disclosed]** Stage 8: broadcast to top 10–30 shards; per shard BM25 + vector, RRF,
   Aho-Corasick (`pyahocorasick`) intent match; group by doc id; snippet; return ~100.
10. **[inferred]** Evaluate with gold judgments (nDCG/recall@k) — mirrors per-shard "Evals"
    (the repo's `evals.py` / `data/sample/judgments.jsonl`).

### Gaps

The shard-learning algorithm; the patented Bayesian dense selector; exact RRF weights/`k`;
harmonic-TF-IDF formula and POS list; dynamic 10–30 shard count; the SQL filter schema;
instruction-evolution algorithm; hardware.

---

## 2. Cybernaut-1: LLM-guided MCTS over search

**Source:** `introducing-cybernaut-1-agentic-search-with-mcts.md`. **cybernaut_mini
mapping:** `agent/search.py`, `agent/node.py`, `agent/policy.py`, `agent/actions.py`,
`agent/state.py`.

### What was disclosed

Cybernaut-1 layers **LLM-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search** on top of Hybrid-3 to build a
search *plan* iteratively — moving from **wide-and-shallow** to **narrow-and-deep**,
explicitly balancing **exploration, exploitation, and inference cost**. Unlike black-box
agents that see only top results, it has full access to shards/selectors/rerankers/signals
and tunes them on the fly. Coverage cited: ~20M new webpages/day. Delivered via V2 Search
API and the `nosible` Python package. **No reward function, UCT constant, action space, or
depth is disclosed.**

### Build recipe

1. **[disclosed]** Use the §1 Hybrid-3 pipeline as the *environment* the search acts on.
2. **[inferred]** **State** = current search config (query text, expansion terms, active
   shards, filters, lexical/semantic weight). **Actions** = mutate it (rewrite/expand/narrow
   query, add/drop shards, retune weights, change filters). Assumption from "tune on the fly."
3. **[inferred]** Standard MCTS four phases with **UCT**:
   `argmax_a Q(s,a)/N(s,a) + c·√(ln N(s)/N(s,a))`. Constant `c` and depth undisclosed.
4. **[disclosed→inferred]** **LLM-guided expansion**: prompt an LLM with current results +
   policy to propose N candidate refinements → child nodes.
5. **[inferred]** **Reward** = relevance (LLM-as-judge or nDCG on retrieved quality) minus a
   cost penalty: `reward = relevance − λ·(num_LLM_calls)` (they explicitly balance cost).
6. **[disclosed]** Anneal exploration: broad/shallow early → focused/deep late (decay `c`,
   grow rollout depth as the tree matures).
7. **[inferred]** Terminate on a node/LLM-call budget; return the best leaf's result set.

### Gaps

Reward/value function, UCT variant + constant, rollout policy, tree width/depth, node budget,
the exact tunable action space, and how the LLM guides selection.

---

## 3. Ensemble & distil → tiny fine-tuned classifiers

**Sources:** `news-sentiment-showdown-who-checks-vibes-best.md` (benchmark),
`ensemble-and-distil.md` (pattern), `fast-enough-to-matter-...-tiny-transformers-...md`
(production). This is a three-post arc: *benchmark labelers → distill an ensemble into a
linear head → replace with a fine-tuned 0.6B model refined by active learning.*

### 3a. The benchmark (what to label with)

- Datasets carved from the index by (year × category × industry) top-N-by-coverage, with
  quality filters (verbatim SQL): `source_language_rank>=0.50`, `source_variance_rank>=0.50`,
  `accepted=true`, `apex_story=true`, `source_is_banned=false`, `media_coverage>=3`,
  `title_num_words 5..25`, `description_num_words 10..50`, `ORDER BY media_coverage DESC
  LIMIT 10` per cell. Tiers: small 10,368 / medium 22,422 / large 43,324.
- **250 hand-labeled** stories = ground truth. Input = headline + description.
- **Identical 9-shot prompt** for all LLMs ("You are a sentiment classification AI",
  reply POS/NEU/NEG, *"when unsure you MUST reply NEU"*, 3+3+3 examples). Full text in post.
- Results vs humans: **Text-Unicorn (PaLM-2) 84%**, GPT-4 74%, GPT-4-Turbo ≈66%,
  **FinBERT ≈69%** (beats GPT-3.5), FinBERT-Tone 53% (regression), VADER-0.10 56%.
  Cost: GPT-4 $0.00983/story; GPT-4-Turbo $0.00329 (2.98× cheaper). **VADER 339× faster than
  FinBERT.** 10M stories with GPT-4 ≈ **$92,000**.

### 3b. Ensemble → distil (the pattern)

Five steps: **Curate → Label → Ensemble → Distil → Scale.**

- **Ensemble (teacher)** by greedy *iterative addition*: start best, add the most additive
  model until none helps. Disclosed trace: `Unicorn(83.6%) +GPT-3.5(+2.8) +GPT-4(+2.0)
  +Sigma(+1.6) +Bison(+0.4) → 90.4%`. Teacher score = **raw sum** of member labels ∈
  {−1,0,1}; discretize `≥1→+1, ≤−1→−1, else 0`. Stability: best ensemble in **51%** of
  1,000 bootstraps.
- **Distil (students)**: encode `"{Headline}. {Description}"` with 35 sentence-transformers;
  fit `sklearn LinearRegression(embeddings → teacher sum)`; **75/25 split, random_state=42**;
  threshold at ±1; score 3-class agreement vs teacher.
- **Punchline**: OLS on **`sentence-t5-large`** = **80.40%**, and `e5-large-v2` = 80.21% —
  both **beat GPT-4 (79.90%)** at ~$0 marginal, ~100× faster. GPT-4 $92k/10M & 57 compute-days
  → student $0 & <1 day. Whole analysis = 198 lines of Python.

### 3c. Production: active learning + Qwen3-0.6B

- **100,000** real-world texts labeled by an **8-LLM majority vote** (Grok-4-Fast ×2,
  Gemini-2.5-Flash, GPT-5-Nano, GPT-4.1-Mini, gpt-oss-120b, Llama-4-Maverick, Qwen3-32B).
- **Baseline** = `SGDClassifier(loss='hinge', penalty='l2', alpha=1e-5)` per embedding
  (6 embedding models), 80/20 split. 86.65% train / 85.93% val.
- **Active-learning relabel loop**: find rows where *all* linear models agree but *disagree*
  with the majority vote → ask oracle **GPT-5.1** (`{"correct":bool,"label":...,"reason":...}`)
  → relabel if oracle sides with baselines → drop the worst linear model → retrain → repeat
  (~18 iterations). Gain: **+3.5% val → 89.48%**.
- **Fine-tune `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`** as *next-token classification* (Qwen3Guard style, no
  classifier head): chat template, **label-mask −100 on prompt tokens**, single-token label +
  `<|im_end|>`, **left padding**, bf16. Hyperparameters (verbatim): `lr=2e-5`, cosine,
  `warmup_ratio=0.03`, 5 epochs, batch 16 × grad-accum 4, `weight_decay=0.1`,
  `neftune_noise_alpha=5`, `optim=adamw_torch_fused`, `group_by_length=True`,
  best-model-on-`eval_val_loss`. **Metric pitfall**: exclude EOS from accuracy (mask −100 AND
  the eos id) or numbers look "suspiciously good."
- **Result**: **87.34%** real-world / **86.4%** Financial PhraseBank, beats FinBERT on both,
  matches GPT-5.1 at orders-of-magnitude less cost. **Serving**: SGLang on L40S, regex-constrained
  single-token decode (`max_tokens=1`, `regex="(positive|neutral|negative)"`, thinking off),
  logprobs → confidence via `math.exp(logprob)`.
- **Open-sourced** on HF: datasets `NOSIBLE/financial-sentiment` (100k),
  `NOSIBLE/forward-looking`, `NOSIBLE/prediction`; models `NOSIBLE/financial-sentiment-v1.1-base`
  et al. — **you can download these directly for the replica.**

### Build recipe (laptop scale)

1. **[disclosed]** Start from `NOSIBLE/financial-sentiment` (HF) or label a few-thousand-row
   corpus with 3–5 cheap API LLMs + the verbatim decision-tree prompt; majority vote.
2. **[disclosed]** Validate the prompt against ~200 hand labels; refine from disagreements.
3. **[disclosed]** Baseline: `SGDClassifier(hinge, l2, alpha=1e-5)` on 2–6 sentence-transformer
   embeddings (`e5-small-v2`, `bge-large`, `all-mpnet-base-v2`), 80/20. Confirms signal.
4. **[disclosed]** Active-learning relabel loop with a strong oracle model, drop-worst pruning,
   to convergence.
5. **[disclosed]** Either stop at the OLS/SGD student (Post 2 — already GPT-4-competitive) **or**
   fine-tune `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with the disclosed script (label masking, left pad, EOS-excluded
   metric). **[inferred]** local `transformers`/ONNX inference is an acceptable stand-in for
   SGLang/L40S.
6. **[disclosed]** Evaluate on a 20% holdout + `takala/financial_phrasebank`; compare to
   `ProsusAI/finbert`.
7. **[disclosed]** Repeat for forward-looking / prediction using the other two disclosed prompts.

### Gaps

Image-only per-model accuracy tables; why Qwen3-0.6B beat ModernBERT/DeBERTa (no numbers);
Search-Feed sampling/negatives-oversampling; per-iteration relabel counts; 8-model tie-breaking;
fine-tune hardware/wall-clock.

---

## 4. Point-in-time knowledge graphs over NER entities

**Source:** `point-in-time-knowledge-graphs-over-named-entities.md`.

### What was disclosed

Nodes = NER entities (ORG/PERSON/GPE/LOC/PRODUCT); edges = statistical **co-mention lift**
within a **single year's** news; every edge date-bucketed so a graph "as of 2018" knows only
2018 — eliminating **lookahead bias** in backtests.

**Exact formula:** `lift = (co / target_events) / (entity_events / total_events)`.
Worked example (verbatim): NVIDIA–Blackwell 2024 `co=69, target_events=2651, entity_events=75,
total_events=2249039 → lift ≈ 780`. A *normalized* lift is used for ranking (formula withheld).
Validation: **24/24** sampled edges in-year across 955 docs. Reference appendix code:
`co_mentions_by_year(events, target_ticker, entity_type)` → `defaultdict(Counter)` keyed by
`event["date"][:4]`, counting each entity **once per event** (presence, not mention count).

### Build recipe

1. **[inferred]** News corpus with dates; optionally cluster near-dup articles into "events"
   first (embedding + agglomerative) to approximate one-record-per-event.
2. **[disclosed]** spaCy NER (`en_core_web_trf`) → per-doc `{type:{name:count}}` — yields exactly
   ORG/PERSON/GPE/LOC/PRODUCT.
3. **[inferred]** Resolve the target company to a ticker via a small alias list.
4. **[disclosed]** Canonicalize surface forms (case/suffix collapse; per-year surname→full-name
   folding).
5. **[disclosed]** Bucket by `date[:4]`; count co-mentions per (company, year, entity) as
   *presence per event* (port `co_mentions_by_year` verbatim).
6. **[disclosed]** Compute `target_events`, `entity_events`, `total_events` per year; score
   `lift`; keep edges well above 1.0.
7. **[inferred]** Normalize with `log(lift)` and a support floor (`co≥3`) since the real
   normalized-lift formula is withheld.
8. **[disclosed+inferred]** Build per-year graphs in `networkx` (ego graph + entity–entity edges

9. **[disclosed]** Evolution matrix (entity × year) in matplotlib: dot size = strength, dot color

### Gaps

Normalized-lift formula; NER model identity; full entity-resolution algorithm; edge thresholds;
entity–entity edge criterion; event dedup (the moat); embedding model / ontology facets.

## 5. Frozen-embedding classification ("contrastive geometry")

**Source:** `the-contrastive-geometry-of-risk.md`. Training-free, LLM-free, **backtest-safe**
classification from frozen sentence embeddings and elementary geometry. Two tricks.

### Trick A — multiclass relevance score

1. **[disclosed]** Author **20 reference sentences per bucket**, near mirror-images (same frame,
   only the class phrase varies), so topic/style cancel. Demo buckets: local/national/global.
2. **[disclosed]** Embed with a frozen model — post uses OpenAI **`text-embedding-3-large`,
   3,072-d, Sept-2021 cutoff** (chosen so it *cannot* know post-2021 outcomes). Two unrelated
   same-register sentences score ≈ **0.3** (the background floor to kill).
3. **[disclosed]** **tanh gate**, band **0.25 → 0.50** (below→0, above→1).
4. **[disclosed]** **cubic power mean (p=3)** per bucket: `(mean(gated³))^(1/3)`; argmax. A
   **dead-zone floor** returns "none" for off-topic (value withheld). Worked scores: local 0.315,
   national 0.417, global 0.739 → global.

### Trick B — binary signed contrast

1. **[disclosed]** **20 mirror pairs**, identical except the flipped attribute
   (single-company ↔ whole-market), topics varied *across* pairs so averaging cancels topic.
2. **[disclosed]** **Common-mode neutralization**: subtract the mean of all reference vectors,
   renormalize. Shared coordinate drops **+0.71 → +0.005**.
3. **[disclosed]** Score = `mean cos(x', set_A') − mean cos(x', set_B')`; sign = class. Running
   example: **−0.068** = systemic.
4. **[disclosed]** Fuse the two independent reads onto a 2-D plane (scale × scope).

**Accuracy**: geometry 16/18 geography, 15/18 scope, 13/18 both — a **dead heat** with
`gemini-2.5-flash` @ temp 0 (identical 16/15/13). Five stated wins over LLM labeling:
deterministic, defensible (re-derivable by hand), cheap/fast, no training data, **no
foreknowledge bias**.

### Build recipe

1. **[disclosed]** Reuse the printed reference sets, or author your own by the rules.
2. **[disclosed/inferred]** Frozen encoder — `text-embedding-3-large`, or a local
   sentence-transformer (`all-mpnet-base-v2`, `bge-large-en-v1.5`); **retune the gate band** since
   the 0.3 floor is model-specific.
3. **[disclosed]** L2-normalize; cosine vs references.
4. **[disclosed+inferred]** tanh gate on [0.25, 0.50] — assume `0.5·(1+tanh(k·(cos−0.375)))`,
   `k≈8–12`.
5. **[disclosed]** cubic power mean, argmax, dead-zone "none".
6. **[disclosed]** Binary axis: `mu=mean(all refs)`; neutralize `v'=normalize(v−mu)`; signed
   mean-cosine contrast (neutralize the input with the same `mu`).
7. **[disclosed]** Verify on ~18 hand-labeled sentences spanning the grid, incl. hard cases;
   optionally benchmark vs an LLM at temp 0.

### Gaps

Exact tanh parameterization; dead-zone value; whether the input is neutralized (implied);
projection method in figures; production axes/thresholds; ablations (why 20, why p=3).

---

## 6. Quant signals: the one template, five knobs

**Sources:** `rebuilding-the-geopolitical-risk-index-from-nosible-world.md`,
`turning-news-into-a-risk-on-risk-off-equity-signal.md`,
`an-embedding-based-approach-to-trade-and-economic-policy-uncertainty.md`.

Every signal is the **same template**: `Σ breadth·weight over matching events /
(total breadth or its trailing-12-month mean)`. Knobs: **(1) concept** (ontology filter or K
anchor phrases), **(2) admission** (`max-cosine ≥ floor`, or ontology AND/OR embedding),
**(3) weight** (`breadth`, `relevance·breadth`, or `breadth·w_unc`), **(4) denominator**
(same-day share or detrended trailing-12-mo share), **(5) post-processing** (rebase-to-mean, or
the full trading stack).

### 6a. Geopolitical Risk Index (GPR)

- **[disclosed]** Geopolitical filter on IPTC **codes** (never label words):
  `iptc_level_1=="conflict, war and peace" OR iptc_level_2=="international relations" OR
  iptc_level_3 ∈ {war crime, genocide, terrorism, nuclear policy}`.
- **[disclosed]** `NOSIBLE-GPR(t) = Σ breadth(e) over geopolitical events / Σ breadth(e) over
  all events`; detrended variant divides by the **trailing 12-month average** of total breadth.
- **[disclosed]** Country cut: `attribution(e) = {main country} ∪ {NER-resolved countries}`;
  group by (country, month) / **global** `B(m)`. Multi-country attribution lifts US corr
  **0.45→0.83**. Correlations: Iran 0.99, Israel/Ukraine 0.96, Russia 0.94; 76 countries >0.60.
- **[disclosed]** Pair cut via self-join into unordered pairs. Iran–USA 0.97, Russia–Ukraine
  0.95; **China–USA fails at 0.28** (tariffs live in the economy branch).
- **[disclosed]** *Trade-coercion fix*: admit if `geopolitical OR cosine(event, trade_anchor)
  ≥ 0.40`; China–USA **0.28→0.75** with only **8,079** events added. *Oil-GPR*: 3 supply anchors,
  keep `geopolitical AND relevance≥0.30`, weight `relevance·breadth`; corr 0.95–0.97. All anchor
  phrases printed verbatim in the post.
- Overall global corr vs AI-GPR: **0.90 levels / 0.79 changes** (raw). 13.2M events, 2019+.

### 6b. Risk-on/risk-off equity overlay

- **[disclosed]** **17 stress anchors** (all printed verbatim), embedded once; truncate event +
  anchor vectors to the **first 1024 of 3072 Matryoshka dims**, **L2-renorm**.
- **[disclosed]** `relevance(e)=max cos over 17 anchors`, gate `≥0.30`;
  `intensity(t)=Σ relevance·breadth (qualifying) / Σ breadth (all)`.
- **[disclosed]** Calibrate: `s=intensity.rolling(7).mean()`; robust
  `z=(s−median)/(1.4826·MAD)` over trailing **252** days; `z=EWMA(z, span=7)`.
- **[disclosed]** **Lag 2 trading days**, execute next bar. State machine: exit to `BIL.US` when
  `z>1.75`; re-enter when out ≥5 days AND `z<0.25`; cost 1bp × |Δw|.
- **[disclosed]** Selected on **2010–2013 only** (grid: exit_z {1.75..3.0}, enter_z {0..0.75},
  min_hold {3,5,10,15}), objective **Sortino improvement over B&H**, 252-day embargo, **plateau
  pick** (median of top-20% cells), then frozen; tested untouched **2015-01-02→2026-06-01**.
- **[disclosed]** Results (test): S&P Sharpe 0.64→0.89, max DD −34%→−18%, return +269%→+254%;
  identical frozen rule transfers to Nasdaq & Russell 2000. Prices: EODHD adjusted closes.

### 6c. Trade / Economic Policy Uncertainty (TPU / EPU)

- **[disclosed]** TPU anchors = **3 topic + 2 axis** sentences (all verbatim);
  `relevant(e)=max cos(event, 3 topics) ≥ 0.35`;
  `polarity(e)=tanh((uncertain_sim − certain_sim)/0.1) ∈ [−1,1]`;
  `w_unc=(1+polarity)/2`; `TPU(t)=Σ breadth·w_unc / trailing-12-mo mean of daily breadth`.
- **[disclosed]** The **signed** axis (resolved↔uncertain) is something the keyword indices lack.
  0.35 cutoff "not load-bearing" (0.30→0.40 moves corr ~0.02); chosen by a sweep vs the published
  index. Scale: **14.9M events scored in ~12 min on a laptop.**
- **[disclosed]** Results: TPU vs published **0.87 levels / 0.82 changes** monthly (the two
  official indices agree 0.96/0.70). EPU = **10 policy "levers"**, 60 verbatim sentences (matched
  uncertain/certain pairs), US-scoped numerator+denominator, category gate ≥0.25; US EPU corr
  **0.77 levels**. Two design lessons: a single generic anchor **fails** (concrete decision types
  needed); resolution must be written as the topic's concrete act, so use **matched U/C pairs**.

### Build recipe (shared)

1. **[inferred]** Corpus: GDELT / open news archive with dates; dedupe by embedding cosine >~0.9
   in a date window; **breadth = distinct source domains** (proxy for `total_netlocs`).
2. **[disclosed]** Embed events + anchors; for 6b/6c replicate `text-embedding-3-large` @1024-d +
   L2-renorm, or substitute a sentence-transformer and **re-sweep the floor** against the
   published index (the post itself set thresholds by such a sweep).
3. **[disclosed]** Apply the concept filter/anchors, admission rule, weight, and denominator per
   §6a/6b/6c. Copy anchor phrases verbatim from the archive files.
4. **[disclosed]** Validation: Pearson on levels + first differences vs the published series —
   GPR at matteoiacoviello.com/gpr.htm, TPU at /tpu.htm, EPU + categories at
   policyuncertainty.com, tariff rate via BEA NIPA on DBnomics. Rebase each series to its own mean.
5. **[disclosed]** For 6b only: the full causal trading stack + train/embargo/plateau/freeze
   protocol above; free price substitute = yfinance `^GSPC ^IXIC IWM BIL ^VIX`.

### Gaps

Event dedup + breadth + dating + topic/country tagging (the moat); the threshold sweeps; why
`tanh(gap/0.1)`; exact daily→monthly + "trailing 12-month" mechanics; Sharpe/Sortino conventions.
No code or raw index values released.

---

## 7. Vector-search substrate & self-organizing tagging

**Sources:** `using-vector-search-to-see-signals-in-company-news.md` (LSH substrate),
`can-faceted-search-at-web-scale-self-organize.md` (entity tagging).

### 7a. LSH-indexed weekly signals

- **[disclosed]** Corpus (Jan 2024): 55M+ embedded snippets; SBERT (checkpoint unnamed);
  **Random-Hyperplanes LSH** — `sign(X·H)` bits → integer hashes → Hamming distance; "300M+
  vectors/s", search over 55M in **<0.20 s**, ~10× a flat FAISS index. Filter-then-search: SQL
  metadata filter → candidate rows → LSH → exact cosine on top N×M.
- **[disclosed]** `get_signal` (verbatim mechanics): weekly Monday buckets; keep sims ≥ **70% of
  max code**; percentile weighting **+8/+4/+2/+1** at p80/p60/p40/p20; divide by
  `weekly_count·8`. **Triplet signal**: for baseline/positive/negative,
  `z=(SMA4 − SMA26)/STD26`; final `=(pos_z − base_z) − (neg_z − base_z)` — works around embeddings
  that can't separate "beat" vs "missed" and around earnings seasonality. Five production triplets
  listed verbatim.
- **[disclosed]** Company disambiguation: **Aho-Corasick** (`ahocorasick_rs`) high-conviction
  seeds → probability model on domain + co-mentioned GPEs → ensemble. AI-news filter = per-domain
  embedding-dispersion × volume → **domain blacklist**. Dedup = shard by time×metadata, elect an
  **apex story** (naive full dedup ≈ 11M s ≈ 4 months → minutes sharded).

### 7b. Self-organizing entity facets

- **[disclosed]** Two taggers per collection: a **fast Aho-Corasick** tagger (real-time, built
  from resolver output) + a **slow neural NER** sampling **X%** of incoming docs. Slow tagger
  proposes entities → accumulate → threshold → **Resolver Agent** (tools: Search, Wikipedia,
  LinkedIn, Market APIs) builds a canonical record (rich JSON schema disclosed: kgid/wiki_qid/cik/
  isin/cusip/lei/figi/ticker/GICS/aliases/subsidiaries…) → **distill** to a flat
  unigram/bigram/trigram pattern list → push to the collection → **retag at next flush**.
- Distillation principle: "the intelligence is in the tokens — distill it into strings + regex."

### Build recipe

1. **[disclosed]** SBERT snippets (`all-MiniLM-L6-v2` / `all-mpnet-base-v2`; checkpoint unnamed).
2. **[disclosed]** **Random-Hyperplanes LSH**: `k` Gaussian planes, codes `(X@H.T>0)` packed to
   ints, query by Hamming (`bitwise_xor`+`bit_count`) or FAISS `IndexLSH`. **[inferred]** 64–256 bits.
3. **[disclosed]** Metadata in DuckDB/Polars/SQLite; **filter then search**.
4. **[disclosed]** Port `get_signal` verbatim (Monday buckets, 70%-of-max floor, 8/4/2/1
   percentile weights, `/weekly_count·8`) + the triplet z-score transform.
5. **[disclosed]** Entity tagging: `pyahocorasick` fast tagger + spaCy/HF NER slow tagger sampling
   X%; SQLite proposal DB + threshold; a tool-calling **Resolver Agent** (Wikidata/ticker APIs,
   cache hard by normalized name); distill to n-gram patterns; retag on flush.
6. **[disclosed]** Facet search: query → facets → pre-filter → hybrid retrieve.

### Gaps

SBERT checkpoint + dims + chunking; LSH bits/tables/multi-probe + the 300M/s engineering;
dedup thresholds + apex rule; AI-news metric/thresholds; disambiguation model form; the
collection-segmentation model; sampling rate X + suggestion threshold; resolver LLM/prompt.

---

## 8. The event layer (the moat) — approximating it

Never disclosed in any post, yet upstream of almost every number. To replicate:

1. **De-dup to one-record-per-event** — **[inferred]** embed headlines/snippets; cluster
   near-duplicates within a sliding date window (cosine > ~0.9, or agglomerative/`DBSCAN`); each
   cluster = one event; pick an apex (earliest or most-covered).
2. **Breadth** — **[inferred]** `total_netlocs` ≈ count of **distinct source domains** in the
   cluster.
3. **Topic tags (IPTC)** — **[inferred]** zero-shot classify into IPTC buckets (embed IPTC label
   descriptions, nearest), or replace the ontology filter with an embedding anchor for the concept.
4. **Country tag** — **[inferred]** NER-majority GPE, or source-domain country.
5. **Event date** — **[inferred]** coverage-peak day of the cluster (post uses this; algorithm
   withheld).
6. **Event embedding** — **[disclosed]** `text-embedding-3-large` @1024-d + L2-renorm for exact
   replication of §6; a multilingual sentence-transformer otherwise (re-sweep thresholds).

Free data sources for the whole guide: **GDELT** (events + source domains), Hugging Face
`NOSIBLE/*` datasets (labels), `takala/financial_phrasebank`, published index files
(matteoiacoviello.com, policyuncertainty.com), EODHD/yfinance prices, DBnomics macro.

---

## 9. Suggested build order for a full educational replica

1. **§8 event layer** on a GDELT slice — the foundation everything else reads.
2. **§6c TPU** — smallest, most self-contained (5 anchors, ~12-min compute, published benchmark).
   Fast confidence that the substrate works.
3. **§6b overlay** — adds the causal calibration + train/embargo/freeze discipline.
4. **§5 frozen-embedding features** + **§3 distilled classifiers** — event enrichment
   (both have open HF artifacts to check against).
5. **§4 point-in-time KG** — NER + yearly lift over the same events.
6. **§1 Hybrid-3** — the retrieval pipeline (largest; the repo already scaffolds it).
7. **§2 Cybernaut-1 MCTS** — the agent on top, once §1 is a working environment.

**One-line summary of the architectural signature to preserve:** *date-partition everything,
freeze the encoder, weight by breadth, normalize by attention, and make every score re-derivable
from counts, cosines, means, and subtractions.*
